#1662. Liverpool transfer news: Agent confirms Andoni Iraola star in contract extension "talks" after strong Premier League start

By Lewis Nolan | 10 Nov 2026 18:21

Liverpool goalkeeper Alisson Becker is in preliminary talks over a contract extension, his agent has confirmed.

The Reds shot-stopper was the best player on the pitch on Sunday, when the Merseysiders emerged as 3-1 winners against Crystal Palace.

That Premier League victory lifted the club to fourth in the table, but Liverpool could have lost were in not for Alisson's heroics.

The Brazilian's contract will expire at the end of the season, though his agent Ze Maria has revealed that he could extend his stay at Anfield, telling WinWin: "Alisson loves Liverpool very much. We are in preliminary talks regarding a contract renewal."

Alisson has been at Liverpool since 2018, and though he is 34, fans are keen for him to remain the team's number one.

At his best, Alisson was arguably the most rounded goalkeeper in Europe, with none of his peers possessing his ability to reliably save shots, collect crosses and play out from the back.

The 34-year-old has been criticised in recent seasons for his kicking, especially after one of his passes against Arsenal on November 1 allowed the Gunners to score the only goal of the game.

However, the Brazilian made six saves and 16 recoveries against Palace, reminding supporters that he is still one of the best goalkeepers in the division.

A long-term contract should be out of the question, but the Reds should look to tie Alisson down for at least two years in order to allow teenager Lucca Brughmans to develop without the pressure of having to immediately start between the posts.

Alisson is not the only key starter set to see his contract expire at the end of the season given centre-back Virgil van Dijk will be a free agent at the end of 2026-27.

The Dutchman still wins the vast majority of his battles against opposition attackers despite now being 35, and he has shown no signs of slowing down.

Only Van Dijk, Alisson, Kostas Tsimikas and Wataru Endo are over the age of 30 in the Liverpool squad, but the latter two have never been first-team starters and are likely to leave.

Keeping the centre-back and goalkeeper beyond this season could be crucial in order to ease the transition into the Andoni Iraola era considering there are a number of younger stars in the squad such as Jeremy Jacquet and Rio Ngumoha that may benefit from their experience.

#1661. Man United 4-4 Aston Villa PLAYER RATINGS: Who looks like the only ray of light at Old Trafford? Whose display was a mess? And which 3/10 star was absolutely hopeless?

Published: 13:52 EST, 8 November 2026 | Updated: 15:31 EST, 8 November 2026

Manchester United will rot 18th in the Premier League table during the international break even after scrambling an unlikely 4-4 draw against Aston Villa.

Michael Carrick's side fought back from a two-goal deficit, inflicted in just four first-half minutes, and went into the interval level after goals from Bruno Fernandes and Youri Tielemans.

They had to pull off the trick a second time after John McGinn's penalty and Leon Goretzka's back-post tap-in made it 4-2 to Unai Emery's visitors.

But Carrick's side refused to throw in the towel despite how hopeless they were for the majority of this game and his substitutes paid off handsomely.

Joshua Zirkzee made it 4-3 in the 92nd minute, teed up by fellow sub Patrick Dorgu, and Dorgu completed the comeback with a 96th-minute finish of his own to send Old Trafford into raptures.

CEO Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox celebrated in the directors' box, all while Emery stormed off down the tunnel before the final whistle.

Daily Mail Sport's NATHAN SALT was in position at Old Trafford to grade both sets of players...

Patrick Dorgu (right) salvaged the most unlikely of points for Manchester United on Sunday

John McGinn (right) was immense but Villa suffered when he went off as they finished 4-4

A mess of a performance. The Belgian got totally muddled up when he tried to save Alysson's first-minute shot with his knees and it flew between his legs. He could then only parry Alysson's shot straight to Jackson, who made it 2-0. Sold short by his defenders for goals three and four but the United malaise seems to have worn down Lammens, who looked so good last season.

Looked like a rabbit in headlights at the start of the game as the ball ricocheted off him en route to Alysson making it 1-0. Did get an assist for cutting the ball back to Tielemans just before half-time but as an overall performance, Villa feasted on his shortcomings.

Looked like the only United defender capable of defending to a respectable level until even he got sucked into the mistake-fest that United put on at the back. A positive first half, in which he made a strong recovery run to deny Jackson racing through for a third goal, was undone when he inexplicably headed onto his own bar under no pressure to gift Villa a fourth as Leon Goretzka turned in the knockdown.

Made a key last-man challenge but otherwise this was another game where he hasn't been able to organise a defence that is crying out for leadership. Forced off at half-time just days after appearing to tweak his hamstring against Roma.

Absolutely hopeless, just as he was against Roma on Tuesday. Switched off in the first minute and made a weak attempt to block Alysson, who scored. Then, two minutes into the second half, he recklessly fouled Alysson to give away a penalty. Many fans cheered when he was substituted. There has to be a better left back solution than Dalot right now.

Thousands of United fans cheered at the announcement that Diogo Dalot was going off

Scored his first goal for United, and against his former side no less. When United were rolling, Tielemans was at the heart of it all. Faded in the second half when Villa took the lead again and he was unsurprisingly taken off as Carrick's first substitution.

Neat and tidy on the ball but got bested by McGinn for the time the Scottish was on the pitch. One of the few who genuinely does look to play forwards when possible.

His goal drought goes on as we rapidly approach a year since his last one. He's electric when he's bearing down on a full-back and he had to score when played in by Tielemans after escaping the sight of Maatsen. Does so much well but his end product simply must improve or he won't merit starts.

Scored a penalty for the second time in a week but cut a frustrated figure for large spells here as the team collapsed. His corner onto the head of Dorgu was the type of quality you need in crunch moments and that's why he rarely comes off.

Looks like the only ray of light these days as this feckless United side fall to even greater depths. Did well to wrestle himself free of Harwood-Bellis to break and win a penalty after a clueless foul from Boubacar Kamara. Stung the palms of Suzuki soon after.

Matheus Cunha dragged United back into the game and did brilliantly to win an early penalty

Didn't do enough to trouble Villa's backline as he once again found himself deployed down the middle. Only took three shots in this basketball-type game.

Could only scratch his chin in disbelief 60 seconds in when Villa took the lead and he looked down and out when it became 4-2 early in the second half. But he was proactive with his substitutions and they all paid off. He deserves credit for that.

Booked for a reckless - and late - lunge. Interesting he got the nod ahead of Matthijs de Ligt at half-time.

Goal and assist off the bench. Has to be the starter at left back from here on out or United will remain in a washing machine cycle of misery defensively.

Drew a furious response when he ballooned a shot over the bar when United were chasing the game late on.

Electric, again. He's fearless and United have needed that this week when the chips were down.

Joshua Zirkzee (for Bryan Mbeumo, 83) - 7

Clinical when the chance came and it was his goal at 4-3 that gave United the opportunity to stage a dramatic late finish. He gives them a focal point that they are crying out for.

Conceded four times and was livid at the end that VAR didn't punish Lammens backing in to him with the last action of the game. It was a performance that saw Suzuki make some huge saves in the first half. There was one big right hand to deny Amad just before half-time and he was also full stretch to tip Cunha's curling shot away, too, just before. Couldn't see Tielemans' equaliser at 2-2 with Mbeumo in front and will feel aggrieved at the finale.

First Premier League start for Villa since his £30million summer switch and he will have not expected for it to come at right back. Found himself in an unfortunate mismatch against Cunha and the ease at which the Brazilian brushed him off shows why it's unlikely to be a long-term assignment given the quality of wide players in the league.

Was so often given the mocking treatment that has now fallen onto the likes of Dalot and Mazraoui during his time at Manchester United but Lindelof is a better player than many here care to admit. Reads the game well and did well to cut out a run into the box by Patrick Dorgu ten minutes from time but was found wanting on the final set piece that triggered the equaliser.

Victor Lindelof is a better player than a lot of United fans may care to admit

Felt like a quarterback for this Villa side for most of it with how many touches he was able to take under very little pressure. Had a big smile on his face for long spells but that was firmly washed off by the end. Abysmal marking as the game entered stoppage time and both Zirkzee and Dorgu scored.

Was given a torrid time by Amad in the first half and still gives opponents too many opportunities to get at him. Shea Lacey had his way with him when he came on, too. Defensively not good enough.

Spent years getting linked to Manchester United but now here as an opposition player, he made them pay with a goal at the Stretford End to make it 4-2. Tidy player.

Idiotic foul to bring Cunha down to give United a lifeline in a game they weren't in 15 minutes in. Seemed to be caught in two minds whether to push onto Tielemans or Mainoo in the 30-minute spell where United looked like a competent football team. Breathed a sigh of relief when the hosts resorted to type.

A total menace that knew within seconds that he had the beating of Dalot each and every time. Clinical strike in the opening minute to give Villa the lead and his trickery and directness paid off a second time at the start of the second half when he baited Dalot into conceding a penalty. Brilliant outing.

Alysson won a penalty after outwitting Diogo Dalot in the United box early in the second half

Best player on the pitch. He made the right decision time after time and even when pressed on the ball when United started to find a groove, he looked to have unshakeable composure. Cool as you like to score a penalty in front of the Stretford End – not least having missed a penalty against Fulham – and then it was his free-kick that led to the fourth. Still feels underrated.

A fearless dribbler that has the potential to be the jewel of this Villa crown in the years to come. In a league that has long ground a lot of flair players down, his physical dribbling through the lines is a sight to behold. Completed more dribbles than any other player by the time he came off.

Quick as a flash to score from Lammens' spill four minutes in and really should have done better when he was played through one v one, only to see Yoro beat him for pace. Led the line in a way that Manchester United were crying out for.

Has never won at Old Trafford as Villa boss and this is the most regrettable of the lot having led both 2-0 and 4-2 here, only to throw it away in both halves. He stormed off furiously before the final whistle.

#1659. GdS: Fluidity, gifts and a tense finale – how Milan overcame Genoa to reclaim top four spot

AC Milan won away from home against an in-form Genoa side to ensure they will go into the international break inside the top four.

La Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below) have analysed a second consecutive Serie A victory for Milan, remarking that if it were it not for the nuisance of the Europa League – specifically that ugly defeat to Ferencváros – they would be heading into the break in perfect spirits.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Still, things have worked out well enough: the win at Marassi, combined with Como’s loss against Inter, has allowed Rúben Amorim’s side to leapfrog Cesc Fàbregas’s team and move into fourth place. It is of course the final spot for Champions League qualification, the minimum objective.

The question remains the same: which is the ‘real’ Milan? The one that put two goals past Genoa in the opening 20 minutes, or the one that nearly threw it all away with a passive final 20 minutes of the game?

Daniele De Rossi almost snatched a point thanks to his substitutions, while Amorim nearly dropped two points due to his own, less-than-effective changes. It seems clear that there is an issue with the squad’s overall competitiveness, with help needed in January.

In Genoa, Amorim opted for a 4-4-2 formation to start, with Yunus Musah deployed as a surprise left-back and a central midfield pairing of Luka Modrić and Adrien Rabiot.

Just seconds after kick-off, Genoa nearly took a 1-0 lead through Osmajic, who surged deep into the final third. Shaken into life by this, Milan took control and built a 2-0 lead.

In the second half, the team gradually shifted into a classic 3-5-2, eventually dropping into a five-man defensive line to hold firm after Ellertsson’s goal. In modern football, fluidity is an asset though it carries the risk of lacking a clear, defined identity.

Milan dominated for long stretches of the first half, particularly on the flanks, but found themselves under significant duress toward the end of the match. The data on the average position of the team is telling: Genoa finished at 55.6 metres, while Milan sat at 44.3.

Anyone unaware of the final score when looking at the stats might well imagine a different outcome, while it remains unclear if the team dropping so deep was instruction or protective instinct. However, the Diavolo survived.

The reality is that sometimes errors – individual or otherwise – have a greater impact on results than good intentions or tactical formations. Genoa arrived at this match on the back of three consecutive victories, though they were missing Frendrup, the Dane who acts as the team’s stabiliser.

Having already enjoyed a string of successes, the team grew complacent. It was a feeling only intensified by the golden opportunity that fell to Osmajic in the opening minutes. Genoa lulled themselves into a false sense of security, and some players began to switch off.

There was an early warning sign when Vasquez gifted the ball to Gonçalo Ramos, though the Portuguese forward’s shot went wide. Later, Vasquez was dispossessed again – this time by Pulisic – sparking the sequence that led to the 0-1 goal: a touch to Rabiot, a cross for Cissé and a finish.

Milan then shifted their focus to the left flank. Under pressure from Cissé, Traoré played a disastrous pass toward Østigård inside the box. The Norwegian failed to clear it, and Ramos set up Pulisic just inside the area for the goal that made it 0-2.

At 2-0, the game opened up for Milan, who favoured direct, vertical play over patient possession. The attacking combinations on the flanks proved decisive: Moreira operated on one side, working alongside Pulisic, who was given the freedom to roam between the penalty area, the final third, and the wing.

The duo of Musah and Cissé dominated their flank against Marcandalli and Ehizibue. Deploying Musah as a left-back was a tactical move De Rossi likely hadn’t anticipated. Was it all over? Had the match been decided? Not quite. Before the half-time whistle, Genoa showed signs of a resurgence.

In the second half, the atmosphere turned hostile, and referee Massa had to send four people off from the benches to restore some semblance of order. Then, a flurry of substitutions narrowed the gap between Genoa and Milan.

When El Shaarawy came on, De Rossi found more space to push forward. When Pulisic was taken off, Amorim’s side lost ground. Ellertsson’s goal – a beautiful strike, aided by a lack of marking from Jashari – set the stall out for a frantic final stretch, during which Milan risked conceding an equaliser.

if you tally up the chances and shots on target, the scales actually tip in favor of the Grifone. So, what does this mean? Is all well that ends well? Is a Champions League spot guaranteed? Certainly not. The impression is that this Milan is still in a phase where anything is possible, in either direction.

A return to the Champions League is far from certain, but the table is tight. League-leaders Lazio are only five points ahead, less than two wins away, so who’s to say Milan can’t aim higher?

Much will depend on January. The winter window shouldn’t be about patching things up, as quick fixes often end up being worse than the original problems. Rather, Gerry Cardinale (plus potentially Markus Krösche) should think about genuine improvement.

It will also depend on Amorim and his ability to shape the squad, ironing out the deficiencies. In the background, the question of Gonçalo Ramos remains. He showed commendable selflessness at Marassi, but he needs to start scoring himself soon.

For now, Cissé is stepping up, having netted his eighth goal of the season and his fifth in Serie A. Roberto Mancini is now waiting for him with the senior national team, which is just the latest step in a fairytale start to 2026-27.

#1658. Brazilian Alysson becomes a starter after injury-hit first year at Villa

By Alexis Pereira | 10 Nov 2026 18:30

Alysson has taken advantage of Aston Villa’s rebuild to establish himself in unai Emery’s side, scoring in last Sunday’s 4-4 draw with Manchester United. The Brazilian winger, who joined from Gremio in January, has overcome an injury-hit first six months to become a starter in the Premier League.

Aston Villa’s season has been defined by resilience. The team lost more than half of its starters in the last transfer window, but Emery, with many signings, has reinvented his group again. They went seven games unbeaten before the current run of four without a win. Part of that change has come from a Brazilian who was already there: Alysson.

Signed in January from Gremio at the age of 19, he suffered in the first half of the year. Three different injuries kept him out of 18 games, according to Transfermarkt. As a result, he only played three games for Villa, coming off the bench against Brighton and Hove Albion and Wolverhampton Wanderers (both in February) and Chelsea (March).

‘He spent more time injured than available to train and play,’ Emery admitted last month about the player’s previous season.

With a full pre-season, the Brazilian was able to change his status and string games together. On Sunday, he scored one of the goals in the 4-4 draw with United, in a standout performance. It is an unlikely story given the right winger’s age and the pressure of the Premier League, where Gustavo Nunes, a former Gremio team-mate of Alysson, has still not made a start for Brentford, the club he has played for since August 2024.

More reliable physically, thanks to a full pre-season, the youngster was able to be available more often and take advantage of the overhaul in Villa’s attack following the departures of Morgan Rogers, Ollie Watkins and Leon Bailey. In his first months he was compared to the Jamaican winger.

‘He has more or less similar characteristics or qualities to Bailey: he is left-footed and plays on the right,’ Emery said in February. ‘And he has huge potential.’

In the first game of 2026-27, he showed he would have more time on the pitch, playing 17 minutes in the defeat to Paris Saint-Germain in the UEFA Super Cup. He then came off the bench in the next eight games, with a short break for a muscle problem in September, and his performances earned him a starting place.

Introduced at half-time in the defeat to Nottingham Forest, he arrived in the box to head in and level the score. Against Fenerbahce, he produced a good individual move on the wing, went past a defender into the area and passed for Tammy Abraham to tap in. Those displays earned him starts against Newcastle United, Viking, Manchester City, Fulham and, finally, Manchester United. Against Viking, he had a standout match for his ability to dribble and win duels, and directly caused an own goal.

At Old Trafford, he did everything but make it rain. He opened the scoring with a first-time shot through goalkeeper Senne Lammens’ legs, forced the Belgian’s rebound for Nicolas Jackson’s goal, and won the penalty converted by McGinn when he went at Diogo Dalot and was brought down. He could also have scored again, but a chip over Lammens went wide.

‘Alysson is understanding things well and is giving us what I want,’ Emery said in September.

‘Every minute he is playing, practising, he is fantastic,’ Emery added in October. ‘We can see his power. We can see that if he can get consistency, a lot of things he is doing: “Wow!”’

The numbers illustrate his role. Villa have been much more vertical this season thanks to the speed of Jackson, Johan Manzambi, George Hemmings and, of course, Alysson. The Brazilian ranks second of all players in the Premier League for sprints, with 22.7, and reached 35.4km/h in one match, the highest by a Villa player and the eighth-highest in the league, according to Sofascore. In the Champions League, despite only one start and 127 minutes across four games, he is among the leaders for successful dribbles (nine, 11th in the competition level with Jackson) and ground duels won (16).

‘Alysson was incredible,’ said Villa midfielder Emiliano Buendia after the 3-1 win over Viking. ‘He is showing all his potential and his ability to play on the wings.’

Because of his age, being in his first year in a new country and the injury history, Emery is cautious with the Brazilian. In different interviews, the Spanish manager has praised the youngster while stressing he still has a lot to learn, especially tactically.

‘He should be a player who can help us. So we need to be patient, seek consistency and be careful with him every day,’ he said on 19 October. ‘This season, he has felt some pain and we need to try to be careful, but also give him confidence so he is comfortable.’

‘Alysson is improving his consistency because he has very good individual qualities, but he also needs to understand the importance of consistency in the collective aspect: defending, attacking, positioning and understanding combinations with team-mates,’ he explained two days later.

Emery remains an admirer and sees the right winger as a possible Brazil international. ‘My expectation is that Alysson can also get there,’ he said after the call-up of Villa team-mate Joao Gomes. At 20, the forward has shown on the pitch what he can do, and if he becomes more consistent, it is only a matter of time before he is called up.

#1657. Kevin De Bruyne: Premier League club ‘assessing real chances’ of signing Man City legend from Napoli

By Oliver Thomas | 10 Nov 2026 18:58, Last updated: 10 Nov 2026 19:01

One Premier League club are reportedly considering a shock move for Napoli and Belgium playmaker Kevin De Bruyne in January.

The 35-year-old spent 10 glorious years at Manchester City and earned legendary status at the Etihad Stadium where he won 19 trophies and made 422 appearances, scoring 108 goals and registering 177 assists.

City decided not to extend De Bruyne’s contract at the end of the 2024-25 season and he subsequently signed for Napoli as a free agent, embarking on a fresh challenge in Italian football.

De Bruyne’s debut campaign with Napoli was stuck by injury and he was limited to only 16 starts across all competitions, but he has since played in all 15 games across Serie A and the Champions League this term, chipping in with four goals and two assists.

The playmaker’s current contract is due to expire in June 2027, but it has been suggested that he could leave Napoli sooner than expected.

Last month, former Napoli striker Roberto Carlos Sosa stated that the “spark never really ignited” between De Bruyne and the Naples outfit.

Italian news outlet Calciomercato have since reported that De Bruyne is going through a ‘mental decline’ and the midfielder make look to pursue a sensational return to the Premier League in January.

The report adds that Everton would be interested in signing De Bruyne and have already initiated ‘first contacts’ with the player’s representatives to understand their ‘real chances’ of signing him.

In order for the transfer to materialise, Napoli would need to be convinced to sanction De Bruyne’s exit midway through the season, and it remains unknown as to whether they would demand a fee for a player with six months remaining on his contract.

De Bruyne is widely regarded as one of the best midfielders in Premier League history and thrived as an advanced playmaker at Man City behind the central striker.

He was also capable of operating as a false nine or in a deep-lying midfield role, dictating play from just in front of the back four, while he also has experience out on the right and left flanks, though he does not possess the acceleration he once had.

At Everton, De Bruyne could be a contender to play in a deeper midfield position alongside James Garner and/or Harrison Armstrong, who have featured regularly under David Moyes.

De Bruyne could also play further forward as a No.10, but this is where Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall has established himself as a key first-team figure with the Toffees.

Alternatively, the Belgian could rivals Brennan Johnson, Tyler Dibling and Merlin Rohl for starts on the right side of midfield.

Regardless of which position De Bruyne would play under Moyes, the midfielder would want assurances of regular first-team football before agreeing to join Everton or any other club should he leave Napoli.

#1656. Opinion: Fresh transfer twist throws Liverpool into unexpected U-turn

Liverpool's first-team squad has changed a lot over the last couple of years.

The Reds have managed to spend well over £600 million on new players with most fans thinking their £450 million spend last summer was going to set them up for a good few years.

However, that couldn't have been further from the truth with Arne Slot leading his men to a measly fifth-place finish.

After this happened, Bradley Barcola, Victor Munoz, Ronald Araujo and Jeremy Jacquet were all brought in to bolster Andoni Iraola's squad.

And, while most of these players have managed to have a good impact on Liverpool, it's still not been enough.

This has led fans to question what's next for Liverpool in the transfer market with an unexpected twist now taking place at the club.

'Good news' is expected to emerge about Alexis Mac Allister's Liverpool future soon

Since the end of last season, fans have known how desperate Liverpool were for a new midfielder.

Throughout the summer, many different players were brought up as potential options such as Lamine Camara, Adam Wharton and Alex Scott.

In the end, none of them were signed with a deal for Camara seeming to be the closest to getting completed.

This left fans rather concerned, especially with how poorly Alexis Mac Allister performed last term.

But, to the surprise of everyone, the Argentinian has been Iraola's best central midfielder this season and has more than made his case to get offered a new deal.

However, Liverpool seem to be sticking firmly to their decision of not offering him one.

That is, until this latest update from journalist Ismael Mahmoud emerged.

"We will hear good news in the next 10 days I guess," Mahmoud wrote in response to a quote from Steven Gerrard who stated that he thinks Mac Allister should be offered a new contract.

Alexis Mac Allister staying at Liverpool means that they won't sign Lamine Camara

On transfer deadline day, Chelsea were just moments away from confirming Camara as their last summer signing.

However, for one reason or another, AS Monaco pulled out of the deal at the last minute and changed their minds.

Many different theories have emerged about why the Ligue 1 outfit did this but, the most common one seems to be that Liverpool made it clear that they wanted to sign him in January.

A deal for Camara is one that makes a lot of sense for Liverpool but, with the club now looking likely to perform a transfer U-turn on Mac Allister, there may no longer be room for the Senegal international at Anfield.

The club already have four central midfielders at their disposal and, while Dominik Szoboszlai or Ryan Gravenberch could both be moved on for Camara, that doesn't feel likely to happen.

That is, especially after each of them agreed new long-term deals just last season.

This is obviously a bit of a downer for fans but, if it means that Mac Allister will stay as a Liverpool player, it could end up being worth Liverpool missing out on Camara.

#1654. Xabi Alonso must look at HIMSELF, not the officials, as another questionable line-up sees Chelsea fold at Sunderland - and Cole Palmer wastes his chance to respond to Thomas Tuchel snub, writes KIERAN GILL

Published: 11:14 EST, 8 November 2026 | Updated: 17:34 EST, 8 November 2026

When searching for why Chelsea were beaten by the side who were sitting bottom of the Premier League, the temptation from Xabi Alonso might be to describe this defeat as a tale of two penalties.

First, Chelsea were denied one when Cole Palmer was sandwiched by Luke O'Nien and Jules Ahoka as he entered the Sunderland area, with the officials concluding the contact occurred outside of the box.

Then, Sunderland were awarded one when Brian Brobbey was brought down by Levi Colwill. The striker had hold of the defender at the same time, and arguably clipped his own heel upon second viewing, but Enzo Le Fee gladly accepted the opportunity to score the game's only goal.

However, it would be wrong to blame this deserved defeat on those two decisions alone. Referee Jarred Gillett and VAR Nick Hopton were weak but not the reason that Chelsea lost.

This was actually a tale of two strikers. Sunderland had one in the brilliant bully that is Brobbey, whereas Chelsea had nobody after Alonso yet again decided against starting Danny Welbeck.

In the three Premier League games played since Joao Pedro's injury – against Tottenham Hotspur, Manchester United and now Sunderland – Alonso has gone with Morgan Rogers as a false nine once and Pedro Neto twice. Welbeck was on the bench in all of those matches.

Sunderland handed Chelsea a brutal reality check as they climbed off the foot of the table

The visitors fell victim to two questionable penalty calls at the Stadium of Light

We are not saying the 35-year-old is the answer to all of Alonso's problems, but he is an actual No9 who scored 13 times in the Premier League for Brighton last season.

Neto was hardly going to have a high success rate when wrestling with centre backs for the long balls which were coming from Colwill and Co. It is a question that needs asking, therefore, especially after another loss.

Why did Chelsea sign Welbeck if not to play when Joao Pedro is injured?

Welbeck came on in the 62nd minute here, but by then, a familiar feeling was washing over Chelsea.

They lost 2-1 here at the very end of last season. Malo Gusto scored an own goal, Wesley Fofana was red carded, and Chelsea, managed by Calum McFarlane in the interim, failed to qualify for any form of European football.

They smacked of an utterly unserious side then, and resembled it here, too.

Chelsea had a week to prepare for this Premier League clash while Sunderland were playing – and losing – to Dinamo Zagreb in the Europa League.

Regis Le Bris' side had not won in the league since August. Yet they were the sharper of the two teams here.

It hardly helped Alonso that Chelsea's attackers never appeared at it individually.

Cole Palmer had a stinker. This was supposed to be an opportunity to show why Thomas Tuchel made a mistake in not naming him in his latest England squad. If anything, he helped make sure those accusations cannot be levelled at Tuchel over this break.

Xabi Alonso tinkered with his line-up and it failed to pay off in a second defeat in three games

Cole Palmer had a stinker in a woeful response to Thomas Tuchel's England snub

Rogers' performance was best summed up by the time he simply sprinted out of play with the ball to gift Sunderland a goal-kick. He and Palmer resembled no-shows.

Sunderland (4-2-3-1): Roefs 6; Hume 7, Mukiele 7, O'Nien 6, Mandava 7; Xhaka 6 (Ahoka 4, 6), Sadiki 7; Meunier 6, Talbi 6 (Rigg 88), Le Fee 6 (Angulo 88); Brobbey 8 (Isidor 67, 6)

Subs (not used): Ellborg, Danso, Methalie, Fofana, Tutierov

Booked: Ahoka, Meunier, Brobbey, O'Nien, Angulo

Chelsea (4-3-3): Penders 6; Palestra 5 (Gusto 62, 5), Fofana 5, Colwill 4 (Estevao 45, 6), Chavarria 5 (Quenda 79); Caicedo 6, Lavia 6, Henderson 6 (Emegha 87); Palmer 4, Neto 5 (Welbeck 62, 5), Rogers 4

Subs (not used): Sharman-Lowe, Barco, Anselmino, Nicoll-Jazuli

Neto looked like a lost little boy trying to lead Chelsea's line in the absence of Joao Pedro.

The half-time statistics said Chelsea had sent more open-play crosses into Sunderland's box in the opening 45 minutes than in their entire games v Fulham, Everton, Tottenham, Manchester United, Bournemouth and Brighton.

Except, they had no striker for Alonso's full backs Marco Palestra or Pep Chavarria to try to find. Just 5ft 8in Neto and the odd other box-crasher.

Trailing 1-0 at half-time here, Alonso made a singular substitution. It was to introduce Estevao for Colwill, who had been tormented by Brobbey.

Le Bris was asked in his post-match press conference if there is another player like his striker in the Premier League. He thought long and hard before answering: 'What do you think? I don't think so. His physicality, his intensity, it's impressive, that's for sure. The build-up is so important to have a target man.'

Alonso chipped in on Brobbey: 'He is not unstoppable. He is stoppable but only when you defend better than we did.' On his own attack, he added: 'We didn't produce enough to deserve to win.'

Sunderland's tactic of hoofing the ball up to Brobbey worked wonders. He scared the daylights out of Chelsea's centre backs. When Fofana first arrived at the Stadium of Light, a Chelsea fan shouted at him as he got off the bus. 'Fofana, please be on the bench,' he said. Fofana may have been wishing he was a substitute as well whenever he was wrestling with Brobbey.

It was the long-ball approach which led to Sunderland winning their penalty. They smashed it towards the top of the pitch and Brobbey bullied Colwill. Sunderland won their spot-kick and, in truth, deserved the lead for the sheer energy they brought to this match.

Alonso is ten Premier League games into his Chelsea career. The honeymoon period is over. Sunderland lost their captain Granit Xhaka to an injury after two minutes here. Chelsea had named a line-up featuring three midfielders. But they never showed any signs of control, and for that, Alonso should be looking at himself and his own side rather than the refereeing team.

#1653. Man United news: INEOS and Jim Ratcliffe make Omar Berrada, Jason Wilcox 'sack' call as Michael Carrick edges towards exit

By Lewis Nolan | 10 Nov 2026 19:11

Manchester co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe still has confidence in director of football Jason Wilcox and CEO Omar Berrada, the latest report has claimed.

The future of several figures at Old Trafford have been questioned in recent weeks given the club find themselves 18th in the Premier League table.

Head coach Michael Carrick appears likely to lose his job after Wednesday, when senior leaders of Ratcliffe's INEOS group are set to meet to discuss the manager's future.

Wilcox and Berrada will reportedly be in attendance, though fans have been critical of their role in the downfall of the Red Devils and have called for their dismissal.

The Telegraph claim that both retain the support of INEOS and Ratcliffe, who has no plans to remove them from their roles.

Berrada and Wilcox were appointed in 2024, with the former having previously worked for Manchester City in a number of departments, including recruitment strategy.

Wilcox took up a role as Southampton's director of football in January 2023, and he was reportedly identified by Berrada as a key talent.

It is impossible for fans to know the true extent of their roles at Old Trafford, but the fact that United have repeatedly failed in the transfer market is a damning indictment of their time at the club.

The Red Devils focused on their attack in the summer of 2025, only for the likes of Matheus Cunha and Benjamin Sesko to disappoint, and there is still no clear left-winger in the squad other than Marcus Rashford.

United signed three midfielders in the summer of 2026, but there are serious question marks about Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos, while Carlos Baleba has struggled with injuries.

Carrick will almost certainly be relived of his coaching duties, and while results and performances suggest that it would be the right call, he has been routinely let down by those above him.

A squad's ceiling will ultimately be capped by how well the decision makers recruit in transfer markets, and the likes of Berrada and Wilcox have left the manager short in numerous areas.

Responsibility for United's struggles must ultimately fall on Ratcliffe, especially as Carrick is set to be the third boss sacked since he took control of sporting operations in 2024.

#1652. £380m = zero points: Big-spending Spurs humbled by Newcastle

These remain the earliest of early days but the blunt facts are there for all to see. Tottenham Hotspur, the club that has spent around £380m this summer in search of instant improvements, have played twice and lost twice in the Premier League. After making eight new signings, they have so far scored zero goals and won zero points.

Not since 1974 has a Spurs team lost the first two games of a league campaign without finding the net. The summer enthusiasm in this corner of north London is therefore already drifting away, to the sound of an alarmingly familiar soundtrack: boos from the home supporters at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

This meeting with Newcastle United was, in the minds of those Spurs fans, meant to be a clash between a team remade by the transfer market and a team broken by it. Yet it was Newcastle, still adjusting to the loss of three key players this summer, who looked the more unified group and more organised team.

It proved to be a truly glorious evening for the visiting supporters, who not only delighted in their team’s victory but also in the struggles of Sandro Tonali. The £100m Italian, who swapped Newcastle for Spurs a few weeks ago, never came close to offering the sort of class one would expect for such a fee. That price tag is not his fault but it is his burden, and in time he will need to shoulder it more impressively than he did here.

Roberto De Zerbi, the Spurs head coach, can rightly say that it will take time for his new group to develop the cohesion he needs. The worrying reality for Spurs, though, is that his opposite number had far less time to work with his players and far less money to reshape his squad. Matthias Jaissle appears to be a man with a defined plan, and an ability to convey it. Newcastle improved considerably after half-time, which spoke volumes of Jaissle’s work. “He is the best signing of Newcastle so far,” said Yoane Wissa of his new coach.

"He is the best signing for Newcastle"Yoane Wissa praises Matthias Jaissle's impact at the club since becoming head coach 👔 pic.twitter.com/dX8nVknpKc

For Spurs, so much of it would have felt painfully similar to last season, when they won only three home games in the Premier League. They played some pretty football in bursts, but not at the crucial points of the game. The second half, especially, was pockmarked with moments of despair. There was Mathys Tel’s free-kick that almost flew into Islington, for example, and Mateus Fernandes falling over when running onto a pass in the penalty area.

De Zerbi said he was sorry for the fans and for the club, and suggested his team is not properly prepared for this campaign. “Maybe we are not ready yet,” he said. “For many, many reasons we are not ready yet.”

"I have no panic, I know very well where I'm going" Roberto De Zerbi apologises to Spurs fans after the defeat to Newcastle 🔊 pic.twitter.com/83DntjG5ZH

Newcastle’s two goals, much like Brentford’s three last weekend, exposed the enduring frailties in the Spurs defence. Anthony Elanga’s opener stemmed from a long pass over the top of the home side’s high line, while Wissa’s acrobatic effort came from a corner kick that Spurs could not handle. Neither strike, it would be safe to say, was the result of world-class attacking play.

Anthony Elanga finishes brilliantly and celebrates just as Thierry Henry did against Spurs 💥 pic.twitter.com/l6qndlMrKm

What a GOAL from Yoane Wissa?! 🫨 pic.twitter.com/mjuHpaa4YY

“After the first goal we lost confidence,” said De Zerbi. “The reaction was not good enough, not what I want to see on the pitch. The solution is not to put the head down, but to react.”

To be clear, Spurs were not quite as bad as they had been against Brentford on the opening day. They did create chances here, taking 17 shots and forcing a few terrific saves from Lukas Hornicek, Newcastle’s impressive goalkeeper. But in the key moments they suffered from the same absence of clarity and execution as they did last season. Troublingly, this seemed to affect the new signings as much as it did the longer-serving players.

Of the five new arrivals who featured for Spurs, Tonali was the least effective. The Italian had been vigorously booed by the away fans before kick-off and the travelling Geordies waited with palpable excitement for his first mistake. Much to their delight, it arrived after only three minutes: an underhit pass, in his own half, which directly led to Micky van de Ven picking up a yellow card. Tonali was outshone by new Newcastle midfielder Nico Gonzalez, who excelled only a few days after completing his move from Manchester City.

"He's got an opportunity to be the main man"Jamie Redknapp praises Nico Gonzalez's performance on his debut 👏 pic.twitter.com/1ga3tsxXHA

Might it have been different for Spurs if £75m winger Savio had been available? The Brazilian was electrifying on his debut in midweek, when he scored against Charlton Athletic in the League Cup, yet was unavailable here due to a minor injury. It instead fell to another signing from City, Omar Marmoush, to lead the attack. He was busy and floaty but never truly hurt Newcastle.

There are more changes to come at Spurs before Tuesday’s deadline. De Zerbi revealed after the game that Richarlison, Kevin Danso and Pape Matar Sarr have all asked to leave the club.

At least the issues facing his players appear clear to De Zerbi. His list of areas to improve was lengthy – he spoke of strengthening the connection between the players, the quality of their play, their work in the defensive phase and the distances between them – but he also insisted he loves them and remains confident in the club’s project. At this rate, though, the fans might not share that confidence for much longer.

The Tottenham boss told BBC Sport: “Disappointed for the result because until the first goal we conceded I think we played better than Newcastle. We lost ball possession in the first half because we didn’t defend in the right way, the distance between the defenders and attackers was too big. We can improve in the defensive phases but today was an unfair result.

“At the beginning of the second half we had some chance to create the potential chances. We created many chances to score, we have to improve the last decision, because that will make a difference. At the end we are disappointed for the result and our fans. We are working to be a great team. When we become a team I think we can change the story of the last two seasons for Tottenham.

“We are working to be good on the pitch, if you believe in work and training then you have to improve day by day.”

Speaking to Sky Sports, Newcastle’s head coach said: “It was incredible and I’m really proud. We are really proud as a club, as a coaching staff to see a team on the pitch delivering the match plan at a high level already, but also seeing players fully committed to what we’re doing. This is a good start and a moment to enjoy.

“We also did well last week against Liverpool, therefore it was a step in the right direction again against a strong opponent with huge signings during the transfer window. This is something we were aware of, but how we handled that challenge was amazing.”

"He is the best signing for Newcastle"Yoane Wissa praises Matthias Jaissle's impact at the club since becoming head coach 👔 pic.twitter.com/dX8nVknpKc

"With the fans behind us, no one can stop us" 🖤Yoane Wissa reacts to Newcastle's win at Spurs! pic.twitter.com/itaiVO3Kx1

After a tumultuous summer, Jaissle has ushered in a new era of hope and positivity at Newcastle, with Wissa and Elanga reborn in attack.

"Oh Jaissle, I can boogie..." 🎶🕺 pic.twitter.com/FmvC2DrLMO

2 - Anthony Elanga is the first player to score in both of Newcastle United's first two Premier League games of a campaign since Alan Shearer in 2003-04.Footsteps. pic.twitter.com/VZ3hXEbpG7

2 - Tottenham Hotspur have lost their opening two matches of a league campaign without scoring for the first time since the 1974-75 season.Concerning. pic.twitter.com/N8izpVYslx

Jaissle records his first ever Premier League win, heaping more misery upon Tottenham, who begin the season with two defeats. Excellent second-half finishes from Elanga and Wissa have given the visitors a superb three points in the capital.

YOU MAGSSSS! 🤩 pic.twitter.com/PRM8yYg7Yl

Barnes attempts to latch onto a ball in behind, but Kinsky races out to claim. Spurs then almost half-heartedly come forward as Udogie tries to find Marmoush with a powerful cross. The new Spurs forward gets some contact on the ball, but it ricochets to Hall, who hacks it clear. Newcastle then make a late change as Toure replaces Barnes.

Fernandes clips a pinpoint cross into Marmoush. The Egyptian shoots via a first-time volley, but his tame attempt is easily gathered by Hornicek.

Van de Ven’s reintegration into Spurs’ defence hasn’t proved helpful. The hosts have been all at sea at the back since the restart. Newcastle showed little attacking ambition in the first half but have ripped Tottenham apart in the second.

Jaissle makes another double change as both goal-scorers, Elanga and Wissa, are taken off for Murphy and Ramsey. Elanga and Wissa have both produced extremely positive displays to kickstart their seasons under their new head coach.

Spurs have looked way off the pace in this second half and Newcastle are well worth their lead on the basis of their performance since the break.

The away fans sarcastically cheer as Tonali is withdrawn for Solanke. The former Newcastle midfielder has struggled against his old club, drastically failing to impact the game.

The visitors are in dreamland! Hall swings in a corner and Woltemade towers above Udogie to win the header. The ball breaks to Wissa, who fires a delightful acrobatic finish into the net, extending Newcastle’s advantage. Spurs’ crisis deepens. They’re on course for two defeats to start the season.

What a GOAL from Yoane Wissa?! 🫨 pic.twitter.com/mjuHpaa4YY

And this time it is another two of last summer’s signings who have combined for Newcastle United’s second goal of the afternoon.

Nick Woltemade won the initial header and got the assist a few seconds after replacing Joe Willock, but what a finish from Yoane Wissa, an improvised overhead flick from close range.

Newcastle needed Elanga and Wissa to be far better this season than they were in their first campaign on Tyneside and both of them have been electric so far under Matthias Jaissle.

As for Sandro Tonali, Newcastle saw this version of the Italy international all too often in his final season at St James’ Park. Good engine, runs around a lot, but does not influence the game in any meaningful way. A reminder Spurs spent £100m on him and have spent almost £400m in total this summer. They have been abject in the second half.

Porro tries his luck from range but Hornicek is there for Newcastle to tip the ball over the bar. The visitors then make a double change as Steur and Woltemade replace Nico and Willock.

De Zerbi makes a triple change as Spurs look to find a way back into this match. Robertson, Gray and Tel depart for Udogie, Moore and Kudus.

Spurs have a free kick in a dangerous position, but Tel slips as he goes to shoot and it flies well over the bar. That sums up Tottenham’s evening so far.

That makes two goals in two games for Elanga, who scored zero Premier League goals last season. It’s an outstanding finish, on the spin while falling backwards. It prompted some great noises from the away end, too, as the ball seemed to cross the line in slow motion.

The visitors have started his second half well and fly into the lead. Nico switches the play and picks out Dedic with a precise long-ball. The full-back cushions a header into Elanga, who swivels and slides a low effort in off the post to open the scoring and send the away support into a euphoric sea of celebration. What answers do Spurs and De Zerbi have now?

Anthony Elanga finishes brilliantly and celebrates just as Thierry Henry did against Spurs 💥 pic.twitter.com/l6qndlMrKm

Newcastle deserved that goal. They have been the stronger side since the halftime interval, and this is the Anthony Elanga that Eddie Howe thought he was signing last summer.

He scored on the opening weekend against Liverpool, but this was an even better finish, spinning sharply and sweeping a shot home on the turn. Smart dance moves for the celebration too.

It all came about from another long diagonal ball forward, but this time it was inch perfect from Nico Gonzalez for Harvey Barnes to put a header into the path of Elanga inside the box.

Newcastle are really growing into this contest, with Spurs getting deeper and deeper. Elanga is starting to get some joy out wide.

The momentum has arguably been with Newcastle since the interval. They’re pushing Spurs back towards their own goal. The visitors are waiting to fashion a real big chance.

Elanga latches onto Hall’s pass, gets in behind Spurs’ defence and beats Kinsky to the ball. However, it was a difficult pass to control and his touch is too heavy, causing the opportunity to disappear. Newcastle are certainly looking more adventurous at the start of this second half.

The visitors make a rare foray forward as Hall bends an ambitious curler from long range that flies off target. That is more encouraging for Newcastle.

Early drama at the start of this half as Spurs appeal for a penalty. Thiaw and Marmoush challenge for a 50-50. The Tottenham forward crashes to the floor as the Newcastle captain goes for the clearance. The referee’s on-field decision is no penalty and VAR agrees. After seeing the replays, there wasn’t too much contact and it would have been a harsh penalty if given.

We are back under way for the second half. Will we see a goal at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium this evening?

Spurs have been knocking on the door and looked like the far more threatening side, but they’ve been unable to find an opening goal. Newcastle have defended diligently and frustrated their opponents. However, in forward areas, they look disjointed and are lacking serious firepower.

⏸️ @SpursOfficial 0-0 @NUFC There's nothing to separate the two sides at half-time pic.twitter.com/ICFqQ3eXMO

Tel has drifted out to the right wing and turns inside of Nico before whipping a ball into the box which narrowly evades Marmoush. Tonali then bursts forward and passes to Porro, but Hall thwarts Spurs’ latest attack by blocking the makeshift winger’s shot.

I would be worried if I were Matthias Jaissle. Newcastle have not looked comfortable dealing with Tottenham’s corners and goalkeeper Lukasz Hornicek has made a couple of good saves this half to keep the scores level.

Much of Newcastle’s attacking play has been aimless, with long diagonal balls pumped forward that the Tottenham defence is prepared for and has tended to deal with easily.

Very little is happening in midfield and neither Joe Willock in the number 10 role nor Yoane Wissa at centre forward has had any real joy in the final third.

It all looks a bit predictable going forward and, if we are being ultra critical, a bit aimless too. They have not forced a save from the Spurs goalkeeper as we approach half time.

Marmoush has become far more involved over the last ten minutes and has showcased his quality with a few notable touches and darting runs. Nevertheless, Spurs have been unable to breach Newcastle’s stubborn defence.

A free-flowing Tottenham move involving Van Hecke and Marmoush ends with Porro sliding a low cross in towards the unmarked Tel at the back post. The Spaniard doesn’t quite can’t enough power on the delivery and Hornicek rushes out to collect.

Marmoush slips a clever pass through to Robertson, who fires in a first-time cross which flies out for a corner. Fernandes whips a corner into the box and Van Hecke wins the header, beating two Newcastle players to the ball. But Hornicek is there to parry the Dutchman’s close-range header away.

Robertson’s deep corner finds an unmarked Marmoush at the back stick. He takes a first-time shot, but his volley bounces wide of the near post. From that range, he needs to be getting that on target.

Marmoush has been on the periphery so far today. Spurs have looked threatening but they could be more attentive with possession at times, especially in midfield.

Van de Ven makes a crucial challenge to stop Wissa from fashioning a shooting opportunity inside the six-yard box after good build-up play from Nico and Elanga.

Newcastle are trying to get the ball forward quickly in this new “vertical” style of Matthias Jaissle but all it is doing at the moment is give it straight back to Tottenham Hotspur.

It has not been a fun first 20 minutes to watch from the visitors who have had little joy breaking through the lines and have invited pressure from Spurs.

The less said about their set piece delivery the better. Harvey Barnes has taken over corner duties from Bruno Guimaraes and has not managed to clear the first Tottenham defender yet.

Tottenham play a short corner and Botman’s headed clearance only finds Porro, who is lurking on the edge of Newcastle’s penalty area. Porro’s catches the ball on the volley, but his strike flies over. The World Cup winner is playing with real confidence.

Jan Paul van Hecke has played a couple of exceptional forward passes in the early exchanges here. The £52m signing is already demonstrating his ability to start attacks from deep.

The Tottenham Hotspur Stadium screams for a free kick as Porro believes he was brought down by Willock on the edge of the penalty area. There’s minimal contact and referee Peter Bankes is not interested, waving play on.

Tottenham stream into Newcastle’s penalty area, and Tonali’s miscued makes it way through to Porro. He feints to send Miley flying, but Hall is there to make a goal-saving block and thwart Porro’s attempt. Spurs are beginning to grow into this contest and are currently in the ascendency.

Tel forces a flying save from Hornicek! Van Hecke picks out Marmoush with a piercing pass through Newcastle’s midfield, allowing the former Manchester Ciy man to tee up Tel. The winger takes the ball in his stride, cuts inside and whips a venomous effort at goal. Hornicek is up to the task and dives to make the stop.

Tonali has made an unsettled start to this game. He’s already given possession away on a couple of occasions and left space for Newcastle to exploit.

Nico then receives a yellow card on his Newcastle debut for apprehending Gray to stop Tottenham from counter-attacking.

Tonali and Tel give away the ball, allowing Newcastle to attack. Wissa cushions Dedic’s cross with an exquisite touch for Barnes, but the winger curls his effort comfortably off target and fails to trouble Kinsky.

Marmoush has been deployed as the central striker on his Tottenham debut, with Fernandes just behind him as the most advanced midfielder. Porro also looks to be starting on the right wing. It’s a very new-look frontline for Spurs following last weekend’s defeat to Brentford.

Sandro Tonali’s first meaningful action: badly underhitting a simple pass to Micky van de Ven. It resulted in the Spurs captain picking up a yellow card. The Newcastle fans are singing a song about Tonali in the away end, but I won’t repeat the lyrics here.

Tonali under-hits a pass back to Van de Ven, who flies in with a late challenge on Wissa, needlessly colliding with the Newcastle forward. The Spurs captain picks up an early booking. That it not the start he would have wanted.

Newcastle threaten straight away as Elanga nearly lifts an audacious lob over Kinsky from a tight angle. It doesn’t quite squeeze into the bottom corner and Spurs get back to concede a corner inside the first minute. Fernandes then bumps into Dedic off the ball, giving the visitors a free kick.

We are under way in North London. Can either side record their first Premier League win of the season after midweek Carabao Cup victories?

Captains Van de Ven and Thiaw lead their respective sides out onto the pitch. The Tottenham Hotspur Stadium is in full voice, with kick-off just minutes away.

With just under ten minutes until kick-off, here’s a recap of the two line-ups this evening.

Tottenham: Kinsky; Gray, Van Hecke, Van de Ven, Robertson; Bentancur, Tonali; Porro, Fernandes, Tel; Marmoush.

Subs: Dubravka, Senesi, Gallagher, Udogie, Bergvall, Solanke, Kudus, Davies, Moore.

Newcastle: Hornicek; Dedic, Thiaw, Botman, Hall; Miley, Gonzalez; Elanga, Willock, Barnes; Wissa.

Subs: Jaouen, Schar, Bamba, Steur, Toure, Murphy, Woltemade, Ramsey, Shahar.

Roberto De Zerbi has explained Sávio's absence from our matchday squad ℹ️📲 https://t.co/ACZscgieFg pic.twitter.com/ddGz2NveX3

“It was bad news yesterday before training in the afternoon because he suffered muscle fatigue and the medical staff obviously didn’t want to take a risk and I agree with them - it’s not the right moment, especially because he didn’t work in the last 10 days, for him 20 minutes against Charlton, maybe it was tough to rest for the days after but for the next game I think there are no problems.”

"Quality." 🤷‍♂️Matthias Jaissle on what Nico González adds to the Newcastle side 💬 pic.twitter.com/yjMBcr0pUm

"If I'm a Tottenham fan, this is the most excited I've been in MANY YEARS"Jamie Redknapp thinks that Spurs have built a strong squad that can compete in the Premier League 👀 pic.twitter.com/55Dwm7BaoE

It is not the sight of their former player Sandro Tonali in a Tottenham Hotspur shirt that will worry Newcastle United.

Omar Marmoush was only at Manchester City for 18 months but managed to score seven goals in just five appearances against Newcastle, including a hat-trick back in February 2025.

The Egyptian has moved to Spurs seeking regular first team football and will go up against the team he has enjoyed facing more than any other in English football.

Newcastle, of course, have a new manager Matthias Jaissle and are playing a different style of football under the German. Despite an unbeaten start in league and cup, the defence has not looked particularly assured.

That could make the ideal opponents for Spurs as they look to prove last season’s miserable home form is not going to continue into this one.

I’m fascinated to see how Newcastle play here. They were happy to sit back, soak up pressure and go direct in attack, mainly on the counter. That sort of approach could be even more effective away from home than at St James’ Park.

For me, it is far too early to say a summer of change has worked for Newcastle. We will have a better idea after this game.

Sandro Tonali’s departure from Newcastle United did not provoke the same extreme anger as Alexander Isak’s acrimonious move to Liverpool or the sadness of captain Bruno Guimarães’ switch to Arsenal. That is largely because nobody will miss him as much.

There is no doubt the Italy international’s determination to leave for Tottenham Hotspur did rankle supporters, especially given the club had stood by him during a 10-month betting ban, but Tonali was only a good player for Newcastle, not a great one.

Nico will make his NUFC debut today 🤩 pic.twitter.com/ilEM8w3Dwd

Roberto De Zerbi has said that Savio is missing because of “muscle fatigue.”

Tottenham had been hoping to see Savinho following his glittering cameo which yielded a goal and an assist against Charlton on Wednesday, but they will have to wait for his Premier League debut.

Both of these teams signed players from Manchester City this week. Omar Marmoush joined Spurs on a loan with a £60m obligation, while Nico Gonzalez moved to Newcastle for £52m. Both players have been thrown straight into the starting lineups of their respective teams.

Tottenham: Kinsky; Gray, Van Hecke, Van de Ven, Robertson; Bentancur, Tonali; Porro, Fernandes, Tel; Marmoush.

Subs: Dubravka, Senesi, Gallagher, Udogie, Bergvall, Solanke, Kudus, Davies, Moore.

Newcastle: Hornicek; Dedic, Thiaw, Botman, Hall; Miley, Gonzalez; Elanga, Willock, Barnes; Wissa.

Subs: Jaouen, Schar, Bamba, Steur, Toure, Murphy, Woltemade, Ramsey, Shahar.

Recent recruit Nico Gonzalez begins in midfield and is set to make his Newcastle debut. Joe Willock scored in the Liverpool draw and is rewarded with a start, replacing the injured Will Osula.

Nico's in from the start! 🙌 pic.twitter.com/wx28WChueB

Unsurprisingly, Roberto De Zerbi has made five changes to the team that wilted against Brentford.

Marcos Senesi, Lucas Bergvall, Conor Gallagher, Mikey Moore and Richarlison have been dropped. In come Micky van de Ven, who captains the side, Rodrigo Bentancur, Pedro Porro, Mateus Fernandes and Omar Marmoush. Savinho is missing altogether.

Good evening from the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, where there is no sign of new Spurs winger Savio. After his thrilling debut against Charlton Athletic in midweek, the £75m forward seems to have picked up an injury. We’ll learn the reason for his absence very soon.

As expected, Sandro Tonali starts in the Spurs midfield. His second Premier League game for his new club comes against his former team. There’s also a start for new man Omar Marmoush, who is making his first appearance for Spurs following his move from City.

Our Spurs side to face Newcastle! 🤍🔢 @krakenfx pic.twitter.com/djFKnl6nsi

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League meeting between Tottenham and Newcastle United in North London.

Following consecutive 17th-place finishes in the last two seasons, Spurs are looking to enjoy a fresh start under Roberto De Zerbi without nervously looking over their shoulder at the perilous possibility of relegation.

Nevertheless, Spurs’ season started disastrously last weekend as they fell to a miserable 3-0 defeat against Brentford at the Gtech Community Stadium. Since that result, Spurs have responded with an emphatic 5-1 thrashing of Charlton Athletic in the Carabao Cup, and also confirmed the signings of Savinho and Omar Marmoush from Manchester City. De Zerbi will be looking to continue this newfound momentum in the club’s first top-flight home match of the 2026-27 campaign.

Newcastle United have undergone a summer of significant change. Eddie Howe stepped down as head coach after nearly five years in charge, while Sandro Tonali, Bruno Guimaraes and Anthony Gordon all departed the club for lucrative transfer fees. Tonali welcomes his former employers to his new surroundings after joining Tottenham for £100m.

Despite this upheaval, Newcastle demonstrated admirable heart in new boss Matthias Jaissle’s first game in charge, earning a hard-fought 2-2 draw with Liverpool at St. James’ Park on the opening weekend. Emotional tributes poured in for club legend Kevin Keegan as Alexander Isak made his return to the club he acrimoniously forced an exit from last summer.

Newcastle looked to be heading for a victory after goals from Anthony Elanga and Joe Willock, until Lewis Hall, who had played excellently, apprehended Liverpool substitute Victor Munoz in added time to concede a penalty. Dominik Szoboszlai smashed a clinical spot-kick into the top corner to rescue a point for the visitors. Newcastle bounced back from these dropped points with a tense 3-2 triumph over West Brom in the Carabao Cup on Wednesday evening.

A first Premier League win of the season is the aim for both clubs by the end of this evening.

Kick-off is at 17:30, with team news on the way shortly.

#1651. Opinion: Liverpool defender who is 'so impressive' given last chance to save his career

Liverpool's first-team squad have been under a magnifying glass for some time now.

Ever since they finished fifth in the Premier League last term, questions have been asked about whether Liverpool actually have what it takes to start challenging for silverware again.

At the moment, it really doesn't feel like they do as they've managed to lose three games across all competitions thus far with one of those defeats coming against Fenerbahce in the Champions League.

This lack of form has forced fans to question whether the over £150 million that was spent on improving the Reds' ranks was worth it or not.

In fact, some have even started to ask for new players to be brought in to try and help them out.

However, since the club still have so many players among their ranks, they have one or two decisions to make before anything concrete can be done.

So, the fact that this Liverpool star is now down to his last chance at saving his career is rather intriguing.

Conor Bradley given six months to prove his worth to Liverpool

At the moment, Ronald Araujo has Liverpool's right-back position locked down.

The Uruguayan's natural position is as a centre-back but, thanks to the Reds' lack of depth at full-back, the 27 years old's main position has been at right-back.

This obviously isn't the first season that Araujo has played in that position as, there have also been several occasions when he was used there by Barcelona.

And, since Jeremie Frimpong is performing rather poorly, Araujo has no competition, which makes his job much easier.

However, in the New Year, Conor Bradley is expected to return from his injury which will add an extra option for Liverpool in defence.

And, since Spanish outlet Diario Sport have now confirmed that Liverpool will wait until the end of the current season to make a decision on Araujo, Bradley now only has around six months to prove why he should be the Reds' starting right-back.

"At Anfield, they are very happy with the Uruguayan, but it is a significant financial undertaking, so they don't intend to make a final decision until the end of the season, despite reports that they would like to finalize the deal now," they wrote.

"If it were today, that would be the feeling, but there's still a long season ahead and no one wants to rush into anything.

"Let's not forget that Van Dijk and Joe Gomez could leave this year, leaving the center-back position, a crucial one in England, very vulnerable. In fact, he was voted Liverpool's Player of the Month for October.

"The player is regaining his confidence thanks to consistent playing time and has scored important goals for his new team."

Conor Bradley has to take this chance and run

If Bradley wasn't constantly side-lined due to injury, Liverpool would be having no problems at right-back.

At his best, the Northern Irishman is easily one of the Premier League's best attacking right-backs with Pep Guardiola even confessing his love for him in the past.

The defender, who has been described as "so impressive" by Chris Sutton is always one of the first names on Liverpool's team sheet when available.

However, with his contract set to expire in 2029, he's got some serious work to do if he wants to extend his stay.

And, the next six months could be crucial to that.

By June 2027, Liverpool will have needed to make a decision on Araujo and whether they want to make his deal permanent or not.

If they do, there's no chance of Bradley making his way back into Iraola's plans but, if, upon his return he can outperform the Uruguayan, he could find himself back on track to getting offered a new deal.

Nobody knows what the future has in store for Liverpool but, whenever Bradley returns to action, he needs to make the most of it and save his career.

#1650. Tuttosport: A ‘different story with the starters’ – how Milan’s win in Genoa proved Amorim right

Everyone expected a reaction from AC Milan after their disappointing Europa League defeat to Ferencvaros, and one arrived.

As Tuttosport (via MilanNews) write this morning, Milan did redeem themselves after their dreadful display on Thursday against the Hungarians. It wasn’t an easy match for the Rossoneri, who struggled heavily towards the end and even nearly conceded an equaliser, but they got over the line.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The three golden points not only allows the team to have a bit more of a peaceful international break but it also means that a spot inside the top four has been reclaimed, with Champions League qualification the major objective for 2026-27.

As the paper points out, one thing is quite clear from yesterday’s match: with the ‘starters’ on the pitch, it’s a completely different Milan which displays quality and an identity. It is equally clear that Ruben Amorim was right a few days ago when he declared that with this squad, the Devils can compete for only one competition and not two.

When the Portuguese coach was ‘forced’ to field second string players to manage energy levels, aside from the win against RB Salzburg they suffered only defeats. The difference between starters and alternatives is evident, and is also evidenced by the fact that yesterday the Milan team struggled towards the end when Amorim was forced to make some substitutions.

After the match, the head coach was once again asked about the topic of effective rotation, addressing the differences in Milan’s performance between Serie A and the Europa League.

“Rotation is necessary for us. Clearly, it was a bad match on Thursday for the players we have: I think it’s a mentality issue, and we have to address it,” he said.

“The only way I know is to work, train with the players, explain, show videos, because there were some things so obvious that I don’t need to explain. I’ll just show some clips of the match and they’ll understand.

“I’m satisfied with the evolution we’re having. We’re completely changing our way of playing. We have more ball possession. We control games with the ball more. I think we’ve had some moments during these matches, really good moments with a good culture. I think we’re far from the end.

“I think we lack time in the final third of the pitch. We control the ball away from the opponent’s area. This is also a key point for Goncalo Ramos to have more clear-cut chances. It’s clearly not Goncalo’s fault. Pulisic is away from the area. Gonçalo is far from the penalty area.

“All these players play far from the penalty area, so I can say we’re still far from the final product, because we’re still working on good progression, but then in the final third of the pitch we waste a lot of time with the ball there.”

#1649. Ghana vs Somalia - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joshua Ojele | 10 Nov 2026 20:14, Last updated: 10 Nov 2026 20:24

Ghana will be desperate to breathe life into their 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying campaign when they play host to Somalia at the Essipong Sports Stadium in the first of their Group C double-header on Thursday.

Having lost their first two matches, both nations are left with little room for mistakes and know Thursday’s result could prove decisive in shaping up their qualifying ambitions, and this makes for an exciting contest in Sekondi-Takoradi.

Two games into the race for a spot in the 2027 AFCON, Ghana find themselves amongst nine sides yet to pick up any points in the qualifiers, with the federation parting ways with Portuguese coach Carlos Queiroz and opting for a change in ideas in the dugout.

Coming off the back of a round-of-32 defeat against Colombia in the World Cup back in June, the Black Stars kicked off their AFCON qualifying campaign with a 2-0 loss against Ivory Coast on September 24, with Malick Yalcouye and Franck Kessie netting on either side of half-time to hand the Elephants all three points.

Playing in front of the home supporters five days later, Ghana failed to make home advantage count in matchday two, when they fell to a 4-2 defeat at the hands of Gambia after squandering a two-goal lead at the Accra Sports Stadium.

Ernest Nuamah and Felix Afena-Gyan hit the target to put Ghana in the driver’s seat, but strikes from Muhammed Badamosi, Omar Colley, and a second-half brace from Konyaspor striker Ebrima Colley turned the game on its head for Gambia.

The four-time African champions have now gone eight straight games without a win in the Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers, a run which saw them miss out on the 2025 AFCON, failing to feature in the continental showpiece for the first time since 2004.

Now tasked with restoring confidence and flipping the script, interim coach Kim Lars Bjorkegren faces a must-win assignment on Thursday as Ghana seek to avoid missing back-to-back AFCON tournaments for the first time since their three successive absences in 1986, 1988 and 1990.

Like the home side, Somalia journey to the Essipong Sports Stadium with the same urgent need for a result if they are to turn their fortunes around and secure a first-ever qualification for the Africa Cup of Nations.

Having edged out Eswatini and Mauritius in the preliminary phase, the Ocean Stars fell to a 2-1 loss against Gambia in the Group C opener on September 25, with Ebrima Colley and Muhammed Badamosi netting on either side of Bilal Njie’s 72nd-minute equaliser to hand the hosts all three points at the Independence Stadium.

While there were positives to take from the defeat against Gambia, Somalia were left spitting feathers four days later, when they fell to a 2-0 defeat against Ivory Coast through strikes from Yann Gboho and Bazoumana Toure in the final six minutes at the Stade Felix Houphouet-Boigny.

Yusuf Ali’s men demonstrated their ability to rise to the occasion against quality opposition last time out when they pushed Ivory Coast to the limit, and they will have reason to believe they can upset the odds against a Ghana side currently far from convincing.

Ghana Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:

Somalia Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:

Newly-appointed Ghana boss Bjorkegren has called up 26 players to the squad for October’s double-header with Somalia, including the Premier League trio of Abdul Fatawu Issahaku, Brandon Thomas-Asante and Ibrahim Osman.

Having missed the first two qualifying matches through a groin problem, Jordan Ayew has been recalled to the squad, and the nation’s captain will hope his leadership and wealth of experience can count for something.

The Black Stars will also be lifted by the return of Tottenham Hotspur forward Mohammed Kudus, who is set to make his first international appearance of the year after missing the World Cup through an injury.

Manchester City forward Antoine Semenyo misses out through a knee injury, while 31-year-old defender Jan Gyamerah, who made his debut against Mexico on May 26, is also ruled out through a muscle problem.

Before their late collapse, Somalia held their own against a superior and more experienced Ivory Coast side last time out, and we expect Ali to name a similar XI on Thursday, with Mohamed Mohamed, Abel Gigli, Ali Omar and Faisal Othman shielding 20-year-old Ibrahim Ahmed Hussein between the sticks.

With eight goal involvements in his last nine matches for club and country, KFUM Oslo striker Nije is currently in fine form, and the 28-year-old striker should lead the Ocean Stars attack once again, while Mohamed Omar, Abdi Sharif and Mukhtar Suleiman should team up in midfield.

Ati-Zigi; Seidu, Adjetey, Salisu, Mensah; Partey, Yirenkyi; Kudus, Abdul Fatawu, Ayew; Thomas-Asante

Hussein; Mohamed, Gigli, A. Omar, Osman; M. Omar, Sharif, Suleiman; Addo, Njie, Hassan

Despite the quality in their rank, Ghana have failed an impression in the AFCON qualifiers so far, but victory on Thursday could provide the spark needed to turn their Group C campaign around.

Although Somalia have shown glimpses of their potential in their opening two matches, the difference in individual quality could prove a decisive factor here, with Ghana tipped to come away with all three points in front of their home supporters.

#1648. Report - It's over: Liverpool finally ready to call Richard Hughes signing a failure

Liverpool are reportedly looking to replace one Richard Hughes signing. They've made an approach and are ready to rule the deal a failure.

Richard Hughes did a lot of big-money business in charge of Liverpool. He essentially oversaw a complete squad restructuring as the Reds looked to overhaul Jürgen Klopp's group and move onto something new.

Now did that work? No. Was it a good idea? No. Did the job even get completed? No, again.

Liverpool have unquestionably gone backwards since Klopp left. Their squad makes use of virtually none of the youngsters who were being brought through in 2024, while the squad also looks very imbalanced.

The reason? Most of the signings just haven't worked out. There are many, many reasons for that but sometimes they're just the wrong player. And Liverpool are willing to accept failure on at least one of them.

TeamTalk reports that Liverpool are now pushing to sign a new right-back. They claim that an approach was made for Pedro Porro, with the Reds in a group of clubs hoping to sign the Spaniard.

Whether that deal happens or not, it's a sign of the thinking at Anfield. They wanted a new right-back, just 18 months after Hughes signed Jeremie Frimpong for the role from Bayer Leverkusen.

It was a deal that always raised eyebrows. Frimpong was a right wing back in Germany and never really showed an ability to defend in a back four. He was also the sole wide player for Leverkusen and that was never going to be the case at Liverpool.

So the Reds were really asking him to be completely different. Shockingly, that didn't work and Frimpong has struggled to establish himself at the club, ultimately becoming a failed signing - despite a ridiculously unfair situation for him.

It's not his fault that Liverpool signed a player and then asked his game to be completely different. But it does mean that the team needs to move on with a player more suited for the actual role.

Liverpool are apparently trying to do that and it's a sensible move. Even if it does mean giving up on Frimpong.
