#1647. Cesc Fabregas's Como win NINE-ONE in the biggest away victory in Champions League history - two weeks after thrashing Michael Carrick's Man United - in just their first year at Europe's top table

By LUKE AUGUSTUS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR and LUKE POWER, SPORTS REPORTER

Published: 17:01 EST, 4 November 2026 | Updated: 17:59 EST, 8 November 2026

Manchester United's 4-1 battering by Como two weeks ago now looks a lucky escape – after the Italian side romped to a 9-1 victory at Lens in the Champions League.

Cesc Fabregas' side put in a stunning performance in a record-equalling win which well and truly announced them as contenders on the biggest stage.

Como now sit fourth in the Champions League standings after also thrashing RB Leipzig and Man United, who are likely relieved that Lens took such a pounding.

It means only Paris Saint-Germain, Real Madrid, and Arsenal have got off to better starts, despite this being their maiden season in European competition.

The lakeside outfit were 3-0 up at half-time – with the scorer of the third goal, Nico Paz, paying his respects to late Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel – before a rout after the break.

It is the latest statement win for Como, whose transformation began in 2019 when a pair of Indonesian billionaire brothers, who originally made their fortune in the tobacco industry, bought the club for $850,000 (£644,427) through their Djarum Group.

Como thrashed Lens 9-1 in a record-equalling victory in the Champions League on Wednesday

Cesc Fabregas is quickly building his name as one of the most talented coaches in Europe

With a combined net worth then estimated at $48billion (£36.4billion), Robert Budi Hartono and Michael Bambang Hartono instantly made Como the richest club in Italian football.

Rather than pursue instant success through lavish spending, Como have built steadily, investing in infrastructure, recruitment, and a clear footballing identity – and it is paying off big-time.

They have now won six games on the bounce, though they still sit fourth in Serie A five points behind leaders Lazio, who have had an almost perfect start.

Their crushing of Lens was the first time an Italian side had scored seven or more goals away from home in European Cup/Champions League history.

And their hat-trick hero on the night, Anastasios Douvikas, is now the top scorer in the Champions League ahead of Erling Haaland.

All of this comes for a side who were playing in the third tier just six seasons ago and on the back of a relatively modest summer spend of £58million on nine permanent arrivals and loanees.

'Today everything went our way,' said an ecstatic Fabregas post-match. 'A great night for Como and our fans.'

There was a poignant moment when Paz paid homage to Miguel and his hometown club, holding aloft a shirt with the picture of the late star alongside the caption: 'Rest in peace.' Though he plays for Argentina, Paz was born in Tenerife and also spent time in the club's youth system from 2014-16.

Miguel died on Tuesday morning less than 24 hours after a collision with Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono during their Spanish second division match on Monday. Having suffered serious head and chest injuries he subsequently suffered a cardiac arrest.

Como's Nico Paz paid tribute to Jesus de Miguel during his goalscoring celebration vs Lens

Despite playing for Argentina, Paz was born in Tenerife and also played for their youth teams

Tenerife striker De Miguel died on Tuesday morning after a horrifying clash with Jesus Owono

Como led 3-0 at half-time with hat-trick hero Douvikas scoring two at that point before Paz's goal and his De Miguel tribute.

Soon after the interval the Serie A outfit crushed any notion of the hosts coming back as they plundered in five goals in a devastating 22-minute spell which included Douvikas completing his hat-trick. Lucas Da Cunha, Marc-Oliver Kempf, Mattia Liberali, Martina Baturina also got in on the act during that period.

Ruben Aguilar pulled one back for Lens before Matteo Papaccioli rounded off the rout in stoppage time. The 18-year-old Papaccioli, who came on in the second half, is a member of Como's youth team and hasn't even played in Serie A yet.

Wednesday's win means Como have broken many records in the Champions League.

The Italian side matched the eight-goal winning margins recorded by Liverpool and Real Madrid in their 8-0 home victories over Besiktas and Malmo respectively. They also became only the second team after Bayern Munich to score nine goals in a Champions League match.

Como followed their 4-1 victory over Manchester United with another emphatic performance, becoming the first team to score nine goals away from home in the European Cup since 1971 – Feyenoord beat Olympiacos Nicosia by this scoreline – as they climbed to fourth in the standings on nine points. The previous best scoring performance by an away club in the Champions League was Bayern Munich's 8-2 win over Barcelona at a neutral venue (Lisbon) in 2020.

Fabregas's side may have made Champions League record-equalling history, but Feyenoord hold the European Cup mark for most goals scored in a single match, having beaten Icelandic side KR 12-2 in September 1969.

Lens, who suffered the heaviest defeat by a French club in the competition, are 33rd with three points.

#1646. MN: Hostile welcome, Amorim’s avoidance, De Rossi’s praise – behind the scenes of the win in Genoa

Some of the unseen details from AC Milan’s win away against Genoa have emerged, ranging from hostility to strong praise.

Goals from Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic inside the opening 20 minutes would be enough for Milan, who were nonetheless left clinging on in the final stages after Ellertsson’s goal. MilanNews have revealed some of the behind-the-scenes moments from the Marassi.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The day in Genoa wasn’t exactly a walk in the park. First and foremost, there was the rather hostile atmosphere created by the Genoa fans towards the Rossoneri. This forced the relevant authorities to ban all residents of Lombardy from attending.

Milan fan groups weren’t even allowed to go to the Aquarium in Genoa’s Porto Antico. It is a shame for so many reasons, and one that reflects the complicated state under which Italian football still operates.

However, there were still Milanisti there to support the team and they made their voices heard. At the end of the match, both Goncalo Ramos and Diego Moreira gave their shirts to young fans in the away sector.

The game could have been a totally different story had it not been for Davide Massa’s controversial decision. At start of the second half, Adrien Rabiot stole the ball, was racing alone toward the penalty area with Cisse to his left, and was fouled by Marcandalli.

Despite the fact it was a clear last-man challenge, he was not sent off. When asked Amorim about yesterday’s specific incident and the refereeing method in general in the press conference, the Portuguese coach responded with a laugh, a smile and a grimace.

It was as if to say: “I’d like to say something, but it’s better if I don’t.” His public response went along this path: “I won’t comment on it, you have the match, because I know that talking about referees isn’t something that could help my team. I just want to help my team, so I won’t say anything about the referees.”

Speaking of press conferences, Daniele De Rossi’s thoughts on Amorim and Modric were very interesting: “I shouldn’t judge Amorim. He’s younger than me, but he has a lot more experience than me. I learn from him. We study him, we watch him. He plays with a system that I really like.

“He puts a lot of quality on the wings, something I’ve also tried to do here. Certainly not Moreira, but with the right proportions and possibilities. I like the way he communicates; he doesn’t blame his players even when he loses, he’s always honest when he loses. He’s doing a great job.

“For anyone who loves this sport, it’s exciting to see Modric play football like this at 41. Last year I had him man-marked, this year he played with two. He has more playing time. Maybe he plays a little slower, but the idea is there.

“We clashed a couple of times and I told him, ‘I don’t play anymore so I can’t beat you up.’ But he’s great, really great. He’s like Rabiot: world-class players. Really beautiful.”

#1645. Opinion: Wonderkid will join Andoni Iraola's squad

Andoni Iraola's time at Liverpool has been recieved differently by members of the Reds' fanbase.

Some feel like he's done a good job with what he has at his disposal and others believe that he should be doing a lot better than he is.

Right now, Liverpool are fourth in the Premier League table and have lost three games across all competitions.

And, while this is slightly better than where they ended the 2025-26 season, it's clear that there are still plenty of improvements that need to be made.

That's why so many transfer links with Liverpool have now started to emerge.

Lucca Brughmans will be joining up with Liverpool's first-team squad next season

Over the summer, four new players were added to Liverpool's first-team squad but, five were signed.

The only player who didn't join up with the Reds this season was KRC Genk's Lucca Brughmans.

The Belgian was signed by Liverpool for £30 million with fans questioning why that much was spent on a relatively unproven 18-year-old goalkeeper.

However, after being sent back on loan to Genk to get some more experience under his belt, Brughmans has brought his game on massively.

Since his return, he's make the goalkeeper spot his own with Liverpool's fans now wondering what their plans for the youngster are next season.

And now, thanks to an update from WinWin Sports, that has been made more than clear.

"Ze Maria, the agent of Brazilian goalkeeper Alisson Becker, who plays for Liverpool FC, revealed the latest developments in negotiations to renew his client's contract with the Reds, in an exclusive interview with winwin," they wrote.

"Ze Maria confirmed to our website that talks with the English club are still in their early stages, saying: 'Alisson loves Liverpool very much. We are in preliminary talks to renew the contract.'

"The agent's statements confirm what the Brazilian goalkeeper himself said, as he expressed his desire to stay at Liverpool beyond his contract, which ends at the end of the current season, confirming his happiness at the English club."

Lucca Brughmans will end up being Alisson's back-up next season

With Alisson's agent saying that they're in talks with Liverpool about extending the Brazilian's contract, it's clear that both parties want him to stay.

And, thanks to the recent performances that he's put in, it's clear why they want that to happen.

On the face of things, this is great news for Liverpool as it means that they won't have to worry about their goalkeeper for another year or two.

The Georgian was initially signed to take over from Alisson in the future but, after his 20 appearances last term, he proved that he wasn't good enough to do that.

This led to Brughmans being signed and, with how well he's been performing for Genk, there's no way that Liverpool will let him go out on loan again.

However, since Alisson is now likely to stay put, the young Belgian will have to become Iraola's number two.

So, not only does this mean that Mamardashvili will have to be moved on but, it also means that the Reds massively believe in Brughmans to meet his potential.

Here's hoping everything works out as Liverpool want it to.

#1644. Arsenal transfer news: Mikel Arteta quoted '£67m' for Bundesliga winger Gunners could have signed for £50m in summer

By Lewis Nolan | 10 Nov 2026 20:41

RB Leipzig winger Antonio Nusa will cost Arsenal in the region of £67m if they are to sign him in the January transfer window, the newest report has revealed.

The Gunners have entered the international break as the Premier League leaders, with their 1-0 win against Hull City on Saturday increasing their lead to five points.

Despite his team's position, Mikel Arteta may hold some concerns about his side's attack given they have scored just 15 goals in 10 games.

Arsenal have been linked with a number of wingers in recent months, including Leipzig forward Nusa, who was reportedly a target in the summer.

The Evening Standard claim that the Gunners' decision to not sign Nusa for £50m means they will have to pay at least £67m in January for his signature.

Nusa is enjoying his best ever season for Leipzig, with the left-winger having scored six goals and provided eight assists in all competitions.

The forward only managed to score five goals and provide four assists in 2025-26, while he netted five goals and provided six assists in 2024-25.

Nusa is 21 and has room for improvement, but his pace, finishing and dribbling qualities could make him a valuable asset for Arteta in the years to come.

The good news for Arsenal is that Leipzig have a history of sanctioning deals at the right price, though it remains to be seen if they would be willing to accept a lower fee in the winter considering they are competing for Champions League football.

The Gunners have long been criticised for their style of play, though Arteta proved last season that his side are capable of winning silverware despite their dull approach.

However, the club are only on track to score 57 goals in the league this season, and they would become the lowest-scoring title winners in the history of the Premier League if they finished first.

Arteta's side should still be seen as favourites for the title, but the signing of someone like Nusa in January would help push them over the line.

#1643. Cucurella defends Vinicius Jr over Diomande comparison as Real Madrid pause eight-game winning run

By Alexis Pereira | 10 Nov 2026 20:52

Marc Cucurella has defended Vinicius Junior amid the Brazilian’s difficult start to the season, insisting that team-mate Yan Diomande does not help him more defensively than the Real Madrid forward does. Real Madrid have paused an eight-game winning run for the international break, during the best spell under boss Jose Mourinho, and are hoping Vinicius rediscovers his form with Brazil under Carlo Ancelotti. Cucurella shares that wish.

Speaking on the Cope radio programme El Partidazo, the Spanish left-back was asked about the poor start to the season of Vinicius, who has just one goal and three assists in 12 matches. The decline in his form, together with a suspension that kept him out of the last four La Liga games, has led to the meteoric rise of Diomande, who has made a difference on the left side.

Beyond four goals and four assists in 16 matches, the Ivory Coast forward has been praised for his tactical commitment, helping Cucurella with defensive recovery. But the Real Madrid number 17 rejects the idea that Diomande helps him more with marking than the Brazilian does.

‘I do not think he helps me more, I think he is more visible,’ Cucurella said. ‘Diomande runs back and is everywhere. Vinicius goes back three times and then, the fourth time he does not run, the ball is played in. If Vini scored three goals per game, nobody would say anything to him.’

Days after his signing from Chelsea was announced in late June, the defender told Radio Marca that he ‘did not mind’ if Vinicius ‘does not track back or help in defence’, because he wanted the number seven energised to have an impact in the final third with goals. Cucurella also told Vinicius that he would do all the ‘dirty work’ for him.

Despite that consent, the forward has helped with the compactness without the ball, following the Portuguese boss’s guidance. The main problem is that, in possession, the 26-year-old has not shown the same efficiency as in recent years in dribbles in one-on-one situations and in decision-making.

Like other figures at Real Madrid, the Spaniard came out in defence of Vinicius, considering a dip in form natural after consecutive seasons among the best players in the world. The left-back also insisted that Vinicius has been working behind the scenes to react and regain his prominence, which he considers fundamental to Mourinho’s success in 2026-27.

‘Vinicius is a player who has been performing at a spectacular level for five years, so it is understandable that he is going through a difficult phase now,’ Cucurella continued. ‘I see that he is motivated and works hard in training, and that is what matters.’

‘The most important thing for us is that he returns to his best level, because if he is at his peak, we have a great team,’ he concluded.

#1640. Chelsea are great entertainers but possess clear weakness

Chelsea are promising to be this season’s Premier League entertainers and yet manager Xabi Alonso seemingly believes less is more when it comes to possession.

Alonso has started with two wins from two league games in charge of Chelsea, with his team scoring seven goals and conceding five. So far, it has been a lot of fun – if not entirely convincing.

But perhaps the most significant numbers are around how much – or how little – Chelsea are having the ball. Having finished their 3-2 victory over Fulham with 38.11 per cent of possession, Chelsea had just 25.6 per cent in the 4-3 success over Brighton and Hove Albion and successfully completed 146 passes. Both were their lowest figures on record in the Premier League.

“The data is not important,” Alonso said. “It’s how you play and what we can do better. I don’t say ‘today we need to have 60 per cent or 20 per cent’. I never talk about those things. It’s about how to prepare, how to be more competitive.”

Chelsea’s third goal against Brighton, scored in the 32nd minute, best summed up the London club under Alonso to date. It took the home side three passes to go from the edge of their own penalty area to João Pedro scoring against his former club.

Jorrel Hato passed the ball to Morgan Rogers, he then released Hato down the left and the wing-back slid the ball across for João Pedro to finish. It was a devastating counter-attack and should have put Chelsea on course for a much easier win.

Joao Pedro finishes off a deadly Chelsea counter-attack and gives the Blues a 3-0 lead 🔥 pic.twitter.com/wAr0ckIgXJ

“After 30 minutes, we are 3-0 and probably, in that moment, we have played too much the result,” Alonso said. “It’s quite normal, it happens in many teams. I am sure in the future we can manage it better.”

It is one thing outscoring Fulham and a depleted Brighton team without having the ball, but can Chelsea do that against the bigger and better teams? We will get an early indicator in the next game against Arsenal at the Emirates.

Alonso’s approach has some similarities to the way in which Antonio Conte set up his Chelsea title-winning team. Just as Conte converted Victor Moses into an effective right wing-back, Alonso started Pedro Neto there on Sunday.

After Roméo Lavia had opened the scoring, it was Neto who grabbed Chelsea’s second goal against Brighton by drifting into the penalty area to finish from Rogers’s low cross.

"It's a nightmare for the goalkeeper!"Bart Verbruggen and Mats Wieffer's collision leads to Romeo Lavia scoring his first goal for Chelsea ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/q5awbdwVV0

"Pedro Neto Pounces!"Morgan Rogers goes past his defender before sliding the ball across to Neto! 💥 pic.twitter.com/WHZCIGsOLl

But whereas Conte’s team gave up little at the back, Alonso’s Chelsea are yet to balance their effective transitional play with shutting out their opponents.

Neto was partly to blame for Brighton’s first goal, as he missed a challenge in the build-up to Malick Yalcouyé’s brilliant volley. Making his Chelsea debut, goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez could do nothing to stop it and can expect to be kept busy this season if things do not change.

“I have come here to challenge and to try and win the Premier League,” Martínez said. “I know the talent we have up front. I try to bring that solidity at the back.”

"Yalcouye with a sumptuous volley!"Malick Yalcouye puts Brighton on the scoreboard with a venomous volley 😳 pic.twitter.com/8UeeyvPjUw

Conte’s Chelsea had N’Golo Kanté to mop up in midfield and that is an area of the pitch that is causing Alonso some difficulties. Manchester City target Enzo Fernández was once again left out of the squad and Moisés Caicedo was not deemed fit enough to start.

Caicedo was eventually thrown on when Chelsea were trying to stop Brighton completing a remarkable comeback, but he was quickly forced off again with an injury. The club have been exploring a move for Monaco midfielder Lamine Camara and that need looks even more pressing now.

“We want the best for the team and that’s why we took a decision [on Fernández] against Luton and today,” Alonso said. “What’s going to develop? We’re not sure. We can prepare. We are preparing for all the scenarios. But I assure you that whatever happens, from Wednesday [when the transfer window is shut] we’ll have a good enough squad to compete in all the Premier League games.”

Chelsea’s new set-piece coach Austin MacPhee had celebrated Lavia’s goal, which came partly as a result of a corner but owed more to a mistake from Brighton goalkeeper Bart Verbruggen.

MacPhee, however, will not have liked Brighton’s second-half goals. It was from a short corner that the visitors managed to work the ball to Pascal Gross and his cross was diverted into his own net by João Pedro.

Joao Pedro puts Pascal Groß's cross into his own net and Brighton have brought it back to 3-2 👀 pic.twitter.com/maBMwVu3DC

Gross’s headed third goal also came at the end of a set-piece, but, fortunately for Chelsea, it was in the sixth minute of added time and Cole Palmer had already made the points safe for the home team before then.

Palmer had done little to impress watching England head coach Thomas Tuchel until he picked up the ball in the 74th minute, shrugged off two Brighton challenges and produced a brilliant finish to beat Verbruggen.

Cole Palmer finishes EXPERTLY to give Chelsea their two-goal cushion back 💥 pic.twitter.com/6xI9W8xe2q

Fabian Hürzeler, the Brighton manager, said his team “dominated” the game, but acknowledged: “I think if you spend so much money on these kinds of players, like Rogers, Palmer or João [Pedro], then, of course, a team like Chelsea can rely on this individual quality. And they showed it in certain moments of the game.”

Palmer, João Pedro and Rogers are clearly going to be a huge problem for Chelsea’s opponents. But Alonso’s team cannot rely on having to score three or four goals to win games. And they might need to have a bit more of the ball.

"The game today was a special game for me." João Pedro says he was happy with his performance for Chelsea against Brighton 🔵 pic.twitter.com/fWSqWo7ert

6 - João Pedro today was the sixth player (and first for Chelsea) to score a goal, assist a goal, and score an own goal in the same Premier League game, and first since Tottenham Hotspur's Son Heung-min against Man City in December 2023.Eventful. pic.twitter.com/xRVjqkOY9D

Fabian Hurzeler turns to his bench for the first time today as Osman comes on for Yalcouye, who was impressive.

We have this news from the Premier League:

Chelsea have two big chances to score a fourth but cannot take either. First, Neto takes advantage of poor defending from Kadioglu and has a shot saved at the near post by Verbruggen. Then Palmer has a glorious opportunity inside the six-yard box from Rogers’ cross but somehow Palmer guides it over the bar. I am going to say it now that I do not think we have seen an end to the goals today.

Fofana is rightly booked for an earlier challenge on De Cuyper as he completely took him out and Brighton now have a free-kick deep into the Chelsea half after a foul by Neto.

Boscagli clips a lovely free-kick to the back post, where he perfectly picks out Gomez, who has a free header from the edge of the six-yard box but his powerful header goes wide of the far post. That should have been a goal and that is a mighty let-off for Chelsea.

Gomez has a decent chance for Brighton on the edge of the Chelsea penalty area but he fires his effort well wide.

Chelsea attack from back to front, with Martinez launching a long ball forward from inside his own box to pick out the run of Pedro into the Brighton half. Pedro ends up having a shot blocked inside the Brighton penalty area.

Palmer was very influential for Chelsea at Fulham on Monday night and, despite Chelsea scoring three first-half goals, he has been quiet today.

Xabi Alonso takes charge of his first home Premier League game in charge of Chelsea as they host Brighton at Stamford Bridge. Both sides were in action in two different competitions on Thursday night. Chelsea reached the League Cup third round as they beat Luton 2-0 at Stamford Bridge, with former Brighton man Danny Welbeck scoring on his debut. Brighton meanwhile confirmed their place in the Conference League group stages with a 4-0 aggregate win over Tromso.

Chelsea began their Premier League campaign last Monday in a west London derby against Fulham at Craven Cottage, winning 3-2 in Alonso’s first game as Chelsea boss. Enzo Fernandez was not involved in Chelsea’s squad against Luton on Thursday and has been heavily linked with a move to Manchester City. Alonso was asked about Enzo’s absence on Thursday and did not confirm whether the Argentine would be involved today.

“It was just because of the game today [on Thursday] and we have other players who need minutes,” Alonso said. “[On Wednesday], in the afternoon. It is a decision that I took. Enzo is a good professional. He is training well and I have nothing to say about this. It was just decisions that we have to take thinking about the game that we were playing tonight [Thursday]. We will see for Sunday [today].”

Brighton began their Premier League campaign in emphatic style as they thrashed Aston Villa 4-0 at home seven days ago. Jack Hinshelwood scored twice in that game but will now miss a number of weeks with an ankle injury. They are also without Yankuba Minteh, who has been linked with a move to Liverpool this summer but is unavailable due to injury.

“When the window is closed I demand from him [Minteh] that he is fully committed to this club,” Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler said. “There are dreams and wishes for players, but in the end we always need to figure out what is best for the club.

“We have had an exchange with him. At the moment he is definitely a Brighton player. It is very important to understand his thoughts but also our planning. As a club we try to develop players. The last few years have shown that the whole environment gave him a lot of trust and belief that he is capable of having this progress. It is always a give and take and he has gotten a lot from us.”

Brighton won both Premier League meetings last season, winning 3-1 in this fixture last September. Brighton have won five of their last eight top-flight meetings with Chelsea. Team news from Stamford Bridge to follow shortly.

#1639. Opinion: Sign him, Liverpool: South American star is screaming 'come and get me'

One South American Premier League star is just begging for Liverpool to sign him. It's time to get a deal done.

Liverpool have a selection of superstars in their squad right now. That's the result of an unprecedented spend over the last couple of years, with the Reds repeatedly breaking their transfer record.

It was viewed as the way to go post-Jurgen Klopp. They wanted to sign as much talent as possible, taking advantage of the position that Klopp left them in, essentially.

The result? It's not a great squad. The talent pool is fantastic, no question there, but Liverpool have been unable to piece things together to create a bigger picture.

It's why we're not sure that Liverpool's next big moves will be for players who glue things together, rather than lead the side. And that simply must point them strongly in one direction.

It's Diego Gomez againWhat do Liverpool need? Well, they need more energy on and off the ball. They need a right-winger. They need a midfielder. They need more space in attack. They could really use more defensive work. Congratulations! You (by which I mean I) have described Diego Gomez. The Brighton star is essentially everything Liverpool need right now. He's a right-sided midfielder who can also play through the middle. Not just as an attacking midfielder, either, but as a covering defensive midfielder, or a box-to-box. The Paraguayan also isn't a superstar who requires lots of the ball. Gomez is happy to take a backseat to others and play a supporting role - and an incredibly strong one.

What do Liverpool need? Well, they need more energy on and off the ball. They need a right-winger. They need a midfielder. They need more space in attack. They could really use more defensive work.

Congratulations! You (by which I mean I) have described Diego Gomez. The Brighton star is essentially everything Liverpool need right now.

He's a right-sided midfielder who can also play through the middle. Not just as an attacking midfielder, either, but as a covering defensive midfielder, or a box-to-box.

The Paraguayan also isn't a superstar who requires lots of the ball. Gomez is happy to take a backseat to others and play a supporting role - and an incredibly strong one.

There is a reason, after all, why Brighton rest Gomez in the UEFA Conference League. He's played all but 23 minutes in the Premier League for the side currently in second and is the kind of player that elite teams thrive with - someone who wins the ball back, makes lots of runs, and pops up with incredible moments.

We've seen two of those this season. The first was a ridiculous goal from halfway. The second was a sensational goal against Brentford this weekend that was essentially a "come and get me plea" to any top clubs looking for that 'glue' player.

We wrote back in August that Gomez is the kind of player Liverpool need. Our Value Adder model is one that pushes him as as an incredibly valuable footballer who's still only 23 and flying under the radar.

Now, he's no longer flying particularly far under that radar. People are picking him up thanks to these wonder goals. But with Brighton almost certainly facing massive offers for their bigger 'stars' in 2027, we think there's a chance to tempt them with an offer here.

Gomez is what Liverpool need. He's worth a fortune to a club like the Reds who are just a player or two away from having a very balanced team.

#1638. Rabiot hits out at refereeing after Marcandalli incident: “Constantly lying won’t achieve progress”

Adrien Rabiot has had his say on the incident that happened during AC Milan’s win over Genoa, in which he was brought down through on goal.

The controversial moment everyone is talking about came early in the second half. Rabiot pressured Marcandalli and stole the ball off him and he was about to surge into Genoa’s half, with only Alphadjo Cisse to his left for company in a two-on-zero breakaway.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Marcandalli hauled him down, yet the referee Davide Massa only saw fit to award a yellow card, and the VAR chief did not deem it necessary to call him over to the monitor for another look. Milan won anyway in the end, but it would have been a totally different game had that been given.

Former referee Gianpaolo Calvarese commented on the incident on his Instagram page and he described Marcandalli’s yellow card as a ‘fair’ decision, which prompted Rabiot to respond in the comments.

“In life, as in football, you can make mistakes. You have to at least be able to admit them. Constantly lying won’t achieve progress, and Italian football is the one that suffers the consequences. Think about it. Bonne soirée,” the Frenchman said.

A post shared by Gianpaolo Calvarese (@gianpaolocalvarese_official)

The relationship between Rabiot and Italian referees has always been characterised by a direct, unfiltered approach. The former PSG man has never been one to hide when he feels he’s suffered an injustice.

He demonstrated this during his time at Juventus. In April 2022, after the defeat against Inter he wrote on Instagram: “It’s difficult to play with 11 against 12.” A year later, in Juventus-Sevilla, he protested again over a denied penalty, even showing the media the marks left by the studs on his leg.

Rabiot brought this to Milan too. After the match against Atalanta on October 18th, for example, he questioned the awarding of bookings, complaining about several uncalled fouls, leading to his famous celebration in front of Chiffi when he scored the 2-0 goal.

#1637. Barcelona Women vs Arsenal Women - prediction, team news, lineups

By Ben Sully | 10 Nov 2026 21:06, Last updated: 11 Nov 2026 10:27

Arsenal Women will travel to Camp Nou for Thursday's highly anticipated meeting with reigning European Champions Barcelona Women.

The Gunners are sitting in fifth spot in the Women's Champions League league phase, while the Catalan giants are flying high at the top of the standings with a perfect record.

Barcelona have made the perfect start to their bid to win a fifth UWCL title, having won their opening three league phase games by a combined 19-2 scoreline.

After comfortably dispatching Paris FC and Roma, Barcelona made light work of their clash against Koge on matchday three, with Claudia Pina netting a brace in an emphatic 8-0 victory in Denmark.

Barcelona returned to Liga F action with a 4-0 success against fellow Catalan side Badalona, before they eased to a 5-1 victory in Sunday's meeting with Madrid CFF, moving them four points clear of second-placed Real Madrid at the top of the standings.

Those two league wins have helped Barcelona build a four-game winning run since suffering a surprise 2-1 away loss against Real Sociedad on October 18.

While they experienced a blip on their travels, Barcelona have won all six of their competitive home games this season, scoring at least five goals in five of those victories.

The Blaugrana have also won 33 of their 35 UWCL home games (D1, L1), including each of their last 11 European home assignments since losing 1-0 to Chelsea in the first leg of their semi-final tie in April 2024.

Arsenal, meanwhile, have struggled for consistency in domestic action this season, with Renee Slegers's side sitting in sixth spot and six points adrift of the top three after recording three wins, four draws and two defeats in nine Women's Super League games.

Having taken seven points from their three European games, the Gunners are at least in a better position in the Women's Champions League, even if their first two performances were far from convincing.

Arsenal required a 93rd-minute penalty to see off Koge on matchday one, before they spurned a goal lead in a frustrating 2-2 draw against Paris FC in the French capital.

The Gunners at least made light work of their home game against Benfica, which saw Alessia Russo net a hat-trick in a commanding 3-0 victory at Meadow Park to become the leading English scorer in UWCL history with 23 goals.

Russo went on to score in a 1-1 draw against Aston Villa before registering a brace in Sunday's 2-1 away win over Liverpool, meaning she has now scored nine goals in Arsenal's last seven competitive matches.

The in-form forward will be hoping to continue her impressive form in Thursday's fixture, as Arsenal look for a repeat of the memorable 1-0 victory they recorded in their most recent meeting with Barcelona in the 2024-25 UWCL final in Lisbon.

Barcelona Women Women's Champions League form:

Arsenal Women Women's Champions League form:

Barcelona boss Pere Romeu remains without the services of Laia Aleixandri, Kika Nazareth and Vicky Lopez due to injury.

Kerolin has also been added to the injury list, having been ruled out for around four weeks with a calf problem.

Renee van Asten, Patri Guijarro and Aitana Bonmati could all come into the side after dropping down to the bench for the win over Madrid CFF.

As for the visitors, they are expected to be without Mariona Caldentey, Selina Cerci, Katie Reid and Michelle Agyemang, while there are doubts surrounding the availability of Stina Blackstenius and Chloe Kelly.

Defender Taylor Hinds is also an injury concern after being withdrawn in the closing stages of the win over Liverpool.

Former Barcelona full-back Ona Batlle is expected to return to the squad after sitting out Sunday’s game with a knock.

Barcelona Women possible starting lineup:

Coll; Schertenleib, Camara, Van Asten, Brugts; Serrajordi, Guijarro, Bonmati; Graham, Pina, Pajor

Misa; Fox, Williamson, Catley, Batlle; Stanway, Cooney-Cross; Baum, Smith, Foord; Russo

While Arsenal are yet to lose in Europe this season, there is no tougher European fixture than facing Barcelona at the Camp Nou, and considering the home side's impressive home record, we think the reigning UWCL champions will pick up a comfortable victory.

Andoni Iraola is the perfect man to do that. He smiles. He is passionate when he speaks and on the touchline as well.

He exudes a lot of enthusiasm and positivity. Even when Liverpool lose he takes accountability and doesn't point fingers at anyone else - especially not his own players.

And that kind of charm can go a long way. Especially when the results overall are trending upwards with the Reds now sitting in fourth place in the Premier League.

More importantly, the club's key players are performing well. Isak has scored double the amount of goals he scored last season already. Alexis Mac Allister is playing like his old self again.

#1635. Ivory Coast vs Gambia - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joshua Cole | 10 Nov 2026 21:27, Last updated: 10 Nov 2026 21:28

Ivory Coast and The Gambia will be looking to maintain their perfect starts to the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying campaign when they meet at Stade de la Paix in Bouake on Thursday evening.

Both teams have collected six points from their opening two Group C matches, and Thursday's encounter represents the first of two meetings between the sides in five days, with the return fixture scheduled to take place in The Gambia on November 17.

Ivory Coast have made an encouraging start under returning head coach Herve Renard, who began his second spell in charge with two wins from two competitive matches before suffering a friendly defeat to Cameroon.

His return opened with a 2-0 victory over Ghana, with Malick Yalcouye opening the scoring before Franck Kessie converted a second-half penalty, and the Elephants followed that result with another 2-0 win against Somalia, as Bazoumana Toure and Yann Gboho found the net.

The Elephants are yet to concede in the qualifying campaign and will be hoping to maintain that defensive record against The Gambia on Thursday, having won their last four meetings with the Scorpions while scoring nine goals and conceding none.

Ivory Coast also boast an impressive home record in this fixture, having won all three previous meetings on their own soil, scoring eight goals without conceding.

While the Elephants have been particularly solid defensively at the start of this campaign, The Gambia's attacking firepower has been central to their own impressive opening, with the Scorpions scoring six goals across their first two qualifiers.

They began with a 2-1 victory over Somalia before producing an impressive comeback to beat Ghana 4-2 away from home, with Ebrima Colley scoring three goals across the two matches, including a brace against the Black Stars.

The West African side will be looking to make it three consecutive victories, a feat they have not achieved in the last five years, with that run predating Johnny McKinstry's appointment as head coach in June 2024.

However, one concern for the visitors will be their lack of defensive solidity, having failed to keep a clean sheet in their last five matches, although they have managed to score 10 goals during that period.

Gambia Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:

However, the Elephants will be without Odilon Kossounou and Guela Doue, who are both sidelined through injury, while Wilfried Singo, Simon Adingra, Evann Guessand and Sebastien Haller have not been included in the squad.

The Gambia have been boosted by the returns of Musa Barrow and Yankuba Minteh, who have both recovered from the injuries that kept them out of the September qualifiers.

Alieu Fadera and Adama Sidibeh are unavailable through injury, while James Gomez has not been included in the final squad.

Jesper Ceesay and Suleiman Camara have also withdrawn because of injuries, with Saidou Khan and Salieu Drammeh called up as their replacements.

#1632. Albania vs Finland - prediction, team news, lineups

By Lewis Nolan | 10 Nov 2026 22:13, Last updated: 11 Nov 2026 10:31

Albania could secure promotion from League C of the Nations League by beating visitors Finland at Arena Kombetare on Thursday.

The hosts are first in their four-team group with nine points from a possible 12, whereas Finland are third with seven points and could be eliminated if they lose.

Albania concerningly needed a 93rd-minute penalty to beat San Marino 2-1 on October 6 in their most recent Nations League outing, and a similarly wasteful evening at Arena Kombetare may prove costly.

It should be noted that while the hosts could secure first place with a win, Belarus are second with seven points and would have to lose against San Marino on Thursday for that to occur.

The Red and Blacks have so far scored eight goals in the Nations League while conceding on just three occasions, and they have kept two clean sheets.

Boss Rolando Maran has only overseen six games - three wins and three losses - but he should be delighted by the fact the national team have won three of their last four matches considering they lost their prior five fixtures.

Albania will hope to win a third consecutive clash at home, but a defeat would be their fourth in six contests when playing as hosts.

Finland suffered a 1-0 loss against Belarus in the Nations League on October 6, conceding the winner in the first minute after an incredible strike from range.

That result left them behind Belarus due to their head-to-head record despite the fact they have the best goal difference in the group, having netted nine times while only conceding twice.

The visitors managed to win 2-1 against Albania in the reverse fixture on October 3, and they have in fact won four and drawn one of their past five encounters with their hosts.

Head coach Jacob Friis's side have only lost one of their four most recent matches, though they have been beaten in four of their last seven games.

Huuhkajat's record on their travels has been poor considering they have been defeated in seven of their last 10 outings on the road, claiming victory just once.

Albania centre-forward Rey Manaj is a likely inclusion given he has netted twice in the Nations League so far, and he may be flanked by Ernest Muci and Arber Hoxha.

Elsewhere, expect to see Ylber Ramadani and Kristjan Asllani together in a double pivot, while Klisman Cake, Ardian Ismajli and Mario Mitaj could feature in a three-man defence.

Goalkeeper Etrit Berisha was sent off in that Finland clash in October, though he has served his suspension and is available for selection on Thursday.

Finland are almost certain to field a similar lineup to the one that beat Albania in their first meeting in the Nations League, with Leo Walta set to start having scored both goals from midfield in that victory.

Samuli Miettinen and Miro Tenho can be pencilled into the backline, while Joel Pohjanpalo is a likely candidate to start up front.

Berisha; Cake, Ismajli, Mitaj; Hysaj, Ramadani, Asllani, Pilios; Muci, Manaj, Hoxha

Hradecky; Stahl, Miettinen, Tenho, Lahteenmaki; Kairinen, Markhiev, Walta; Svanback, Pohjanpalo, Hakans

Thursday's clash will almost certainly be closely fought, and both teams will likely create opportunities.

However, it is difficult to ignore Finland's inconsistencies on the road, and given Albania have improved considerably at home, the hosts should be seen as favourites at Arena Kombetare.

#1630. Report: Liverpool enter transfer battle with Barcelona for €25m star

Liverpool have been linked with a whole host of players ahead of the winter transfer window.

Many areas among their ranks need upgrading and, even though fans knew this during the summer, Liverpool still only signed four new players.

And, one of them (Jeremy Jacquet) was already confirmed all the way back in January.

Now that we're a few months into the season, it's clear that some cracks are starting to show among the Reds' ranks.

So, with the January transfer window now edging closer, the rumour mill is likely to go into overdrive.

Liverpool and Barcelona have both set their eyes on Juventus' Andrea Cambiaso

Liverpool's full-backs have been a major problem for them this term.

Left-back has been the main issue but, there have been times when some dodgy situations have occurred at right-back.

Indeed, Ronald Araujo has performed much better than Kostas Tsimikas or Milos Kerkez have all season but, it still feels like an upgrade could be beneficial, or, at least someone with a bit of a higher ceiling than the Uruguayan needs to be brought in.

Because, while the defender is good, he's going to be 28 years old by June 2027 which is usually when the performance levels of players start to drop.

So, that's why this latest news from TuttoJuve should pique the interest of fans.

"Barcelona aren't the only team to have included Cambiaso on their list of targets," they wrote.

"Liverpool and Manchester United have also reportedly expressed interest in the Italian full-back, who is particularly appreciated for his ability to cover multiple roles on the wings.

"In particular, Manchester United are reportedly evaluating reinforcements for the left side of defence, while Liverpool are reportedly continuing to monitor various profiles to broaden their options.

"Cambiaso's versatility, which allows him to play on both flanks and in different playing systems, represents a particularly attractive characteristic for major European clubs.

"But one question remains: would €20-25 million be enough to convince Juventus to give up on a player with these characteristics?"

Andrea Cambiaso's versatility is a major selling point for the Italian

Versatility has become a key part of football in recent years.

Clubs now need players to be able to play in multiple positions if needed.

Because, with the sheer number of injuries that they suffer, having just one back-up option for each position isn't really enough anymore.

Cambiaso has been a regular feature for Juventus over the last few years and his ability to play on either side of the pitch is massively beneficial to any club that signs him.

The Italy international is also only 26 years old so, while he already has a lot of experience under his belt, there is still room for him to improve.

Right now, it's unclear what the future holds for Cambiaso but, if Liverpool are serious about reigniting their interest in him, they're going to have to be quick, especially with Barcelona lurking.

#1629. Senegal vs Sudan - prediction, team news, lineups

By Nsidibe Akpan | 10 Nov 2026 23:08, Last updated: 11 Nov 2026 10:22

Senegal host Sudan in Group J of 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying at Stade Leopold Sedar Senghor in Dakar on Thursday.

The Lions of Teranga are unbeaten but have scored only twice in two games, while the Falcons of Jediane arrive third on three points after a 4-1 defeat in Maputo.

Senegal are second in Group J on four points, level with Mozambique but behind them on goal difference, +1 to +3.

Patrick Vieira's first competitive game in charge ended 1-1 away to Mozambique on September 25, and Senegal then edged Ethiopia 1-0 in Bahir Dar four days later through Ibrahim Mbaye's 11th-minute goal despite 61% possession.

The 1-0 friendly win over Comoros in Marseille on October 4, settled by Iliman Ndiaye's fifth-minute goal, made it three games in a row with a single Senegal goal and only one conceded across them.

Off the pitch, Ismail Jakobs has retired from international football, and Sadio Mane asked to be excused from the squad to stay home with his family.

Vieira's second squad includes four first call-ups, Pathe Mboup, Pape Demba Diop, Clayton Diandy and Paul Mendy, and does not include Idrissa Gana Gueye.

Senegal have not lost in eight meetings with Sudan, winning five and drawing three, the latest a 3-1 victory in the Africa Cup of Nations last 16 in Tangier on January 3 in which Pape Gueye scored twice before half time.

Sudan are third in Group J on three points with two goals scored and four conceded, and both of their goals have come from penalties.

Mohamed Eisa converted an 86th-minute penalty to beat Ethiopia 1-0 in Juba, the capital of South Sudan, on September 25, a result that briefly took the Falcons of Jediane top of the group.

Mozambique then won 4-1 in Maputo on September 29, with Witi scoring in the 24th minute, Chamito adding a brace, Guima making it 3-0 in the 58th minute and Yaser Hamed pulling one back from the spot in the 88th.

Kwesi Appiah, the Ghanaian head coach, took Sudan to the last 16 of the January tournament, where Abdallah, a semi-professional at an Australian second-tier club in Melbourne, gave them a sixth-minute lead before Senegal replied three times.

Several of Appiah's players come from Al Hilal and Al Merrikh, and the return leg against Senegal follows on Monday, November 16.

Sudan Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:

Krepin Diatta was forced off in Watford's Championship match against Middlesbrough on November 7 and has been replaced in the squad by the Sevilla defender Arouna Sangante.

Habib Diarra, Ismaila Sarr and Abdallah Sima are also unavailable, which leaves Nicolas Jackson, Mbaye, Ndiaye and Boulaye Dia as the main attacking options.

With Jakobs retired, El Hadji Malick Diouf is the left-back option, and Kalidou Koulibaly captains a back line that also includes Moussa Niakhate.

For the visitors, no injury or suspension has been reported ahead of the trip to Dakar.

Mohamed Eisa and Yasin Hamed have found the back of the net from the spot against Ethiopia and Mozambique respectively, and will hope to get a goal from open play against Senegal.

Absences such as Mane, Diatta and Sarr thin the squad, yet the Koulibaly and Niakhate pairing remains intact and should be enough to keep out a Sudan attack whose only goals so far came from the penalty spot.

#1628. Manchester United’s attack may be their best form of defence this season

Is attack going to be Manchester United’s best form of defence this season?

There was plenty to like going forward, particularly once United had nudged their way in front after their second lucky break of what had hitherto looked like being a tricky afternoon.

Give this team a little space and they have the attacking players to inflict some serious damage, none more so than Bruno Fernandes who, just five days after collecting the PFA Players’ Player of the Year award, scored a hat-trick in what was another inspired performance.

Ipswich Town will testify to that after a sobering second half when it felt like United were going to score with every raid forward and, for a time, even threaten to equal the nine goals they scored against the promoted side at this ground 31 years ago.

In the returning Marcus Rashford, whom manager Michael Carrick likened to a “new signing”, Matheus Cunha, Bryan Mbeumo and, of course, Fernandes, United have an intriguing blend of attacking players. Throw in Kobbie Mainoo who, on another day, would have stolen the headlines with an imperious display in central midfield, and one thing United are not lacking for is creativity.

Their offensive problems tend to come when opponents sit in and ask to be broken down. Hull City, of course, proved as much last weekend when United looked desperately short of ideas in attack.

But you would probably bet on Carrick being more likely to find solutions to that particular conundrum than some of the defensive headaches that again reared their head here.

A week after that shock 2-0 defeat to Hull, United were given another scare when Ipswich took advantage of more meek defending to lead and could easily have scored more in that first half.

With a couple of days of the transfer window still remaining, it would feel remiss of United not to add a quality left-back before the deadline passes.

Those 15 minutes in the first half when Abdul Fatawu gave Luke Shaw a torrid time, not least in that moment he raced away from the United defender to cross for Leif Davis to score, should tell United’s hierarchy everything about the risks of not reinforcing in the position.

Ipswich STUN Old Trafford! Leif Davis does superbly to volley past Senne Lammens and give Gary O'Neil's side the lead 💥 pic.twitter.com/sJ0XNf8OiT

Defensive rebuilding is next summer’s big project but some things cannot wait and that is before we get to some of the issues in the other full-back position, which Ipswich also exploited. Fatawu aside, Daizen Maeda and Davis caused Diogo Dalot and Mbeumo problems down United’s right and the excellent Julio Enciso was a persistent nuisance until the game fell away from Ipswich.

For all the defensive concerns, though, United were exhilarating going forward, especially once they found themselves in front after benefiting from a curious ruling that dictated Harry Maguire’s “accidental” handball in the lead-up to the home team’s second goal was “not punishable” because he did not end up scoring.

In other words, had Maguire himself found the net and not seen his cross-cum-shot deflect in off the Ipswich defender Jacob Greaves, the goal would not have stood.

Harry Maguire's shot cannons in off Jacob Greaves and Manchester United are in front at Old Trafford after a VAR review! 💪 pic.twitter.com/hUdogDQX6k

United were brilliant from that point on. There had been flashes of the threat they hold in the opening 45 minutes but thereafter Ipswich just found themselves routinely bludgeoned and unable to escape the tailspin. As the rain poured down, the goals poured in. Gary O’Neil, the Ipswich manager, talked about a lack of “emotional discipline” but plenty of teams would have found United hard to contain in that moment.

Rashford was a threat on his first start for United for 626 days. Harness his talent in the right way and he will be an enormous asset. Cunha’s withdrawn role, with Fernandes and Mbeumo routinely racing in behind United’s false nine, caused Ipswich no end of problems. Amad Diallo and Mason Mount were missing through injury and Benjamin Sesko, a substitute, is still working his way back to fitness after missing all of pre-season. Patrick Dorgu almost scored a couple after coming on. So Carrick has plenty of options.

Fernandes was at his irrepressible best, initially punishing poor Marcelino Núñez after his slip allowed Cunha to play in the United captain to equalise five minutes before the restart and then taking the game away from Ipswich in the second.

Bruno Fernandes equalises for Manchester United! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/CdEI1REeUD

After missing two penalties in pre-season, he made no mistake from the spot after Greaves had brought down Cunha. He then steered home a close-range finish after Mbeumo’s shot was blocked and almost lobbed the Ipswich goalkeeper Kjell Scherpen from 60 yards. His last act was to send Mbeumo through to score with a delicious lob.

"He's the prince of this place!"Bruno Fernandes completes his hat-trick 🎩 pic.twitter.com/KgLlaMcKGR

This was the first time United had scored five goals in a Premier League game since beating Leeds United five years ago and you had to go back 10 years to find the last time they had more shots in a league match.

“There was a good mixture [in attack] there,” Carrick said. “Obviously we’ve got to find the right balance and options. We can play slightly different ways across the front line and a lot of the front players can play different roles.

“It was a little bit different today playing Cunha a bit deeper, and Bryan and Marcus a little bit higher. So it’s up to us to try and get that balance right, but certainly there’s creation and there’s goals within the squad, for sure.”

There was little doubt United benefited from the return of Mainoo in midfield. Summer signing Andrey Santos was the one to make way and Mainoo in turn produced the kind of intelligent, inventive display alongside Youri Tielemans that makes you wonder how Thomas Tuchel did not give the midfielder a minute for England at this summer’s World Cup.

He recycles possession beautifully, excels in the tight spaces, has a nose for goal and an eye for a pass and a lovely ability to glide past players even though he is not quick. Ipswich could not live with him.

Asked where Mainoo could still develop, Carrick said, half in jest: “On today’s performance, not much, really. I thought he was pretty much all-around, very, very good for a first start back. I understand Bruno will get a lot of credit today, and he deserves that as well, but I thought Kobbie was immense in the middle of the pitch for us and underpinned the performance of the team.”

The Man Utd head coach told Sky Sports: “It was a good win. It was a really good win in the end. We played some really good football. The biggest thing today was the mentality of the boys tp overcomes setbacks. We’re going to have them and it depends on how you deal with them. I was really pleased with that. It’s easy to look at the result but the mentality and the stubbornness really pleased me.

“We controlled the game pretty well for the most part. A lot of our play was looking on the way to how we wanted it to look. The boys took it on really well and we were fabulous.”

And on Bruno Fernandes, Carrick added: “He showed his quality today. Bruno did what he’s good at. He’s had a big week winning awards. Three goals and a fantastic performance.

“There were a lot of positives with and without the ball but it’s the whole mentality dealing with it and trusting each other. Last week didn’t go for us and we accept that. Today was a lot better.

“We’re not getting carried away. We were down last week but everything wasn’t wrong. We can still get better, we haven’t cracked it. We’ll get ready for the next.”

Speaking with Sky Sports, he said: “Really unlucky to be 2-1 down, really unlucky - two of the most unlucky goals you will see, but then not good enough to get back into it. We got punished by a very good side.

“To beat Manchester United at Old Trafford you need the moments to go in your favour and they didn’t. Rules can go against you, or a deflection, there are lots of things that can happen in a game that are beyond your control.

“It is a complicated rule - handball if it’s the goal scorer but not if it takes a deflection and was heading off the target. I think that is tough for a referee.

“But no problem. I’m not here to moan about refs. We get no points, at Old Trafford a lot of people leave with no points but we leave with an understanding of where to get better.

“We have three points from two tough games. A good start for us. It is the Premier League, the lads understand there will be highs and lows. We don’t want there to be too many lows but the lads are fine in there. They understand.”

"I understand the rules, but it doesn't feel right" Ashley Young and Darren Bent react to the reasoning behind Harry Maguire's potential handball not being given 🎙️ pic.twitter.com/MGJdBNhbYx

"We deserved that little bit of luck"Harry Maguire discusses Manchester United's controversial second goal where he appeared to handle the ball 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/AY3vWRCxZZ

The hat-trick hero told Sky Sports: “It was a massive result for us. We lost three points last week. First game at home, the fans have been waiting for this. It’s not to make up for last week, you can’t get six points from it. Second half we were very good.

“Scoring before half-time is always important if it’s to get on top of the game or draw the game. We were in control of the game. In the second half, we were very good.

“Scoring goals is the best feeling in football. Doing a half-time at home with our fans is something I’m proud of. I hope I can do much more and help my team-mate score goals too.”

Mission accomplished, boss 👏 https://t.co/0BGBtMYg3H pic.twitter.com/dN0DayO283

Bruno Fernandes brilliance 🌟🌟🌟 pic.twitter.com/96LiCipQKk

Fernandes stars with a second-half hat-trick as Man Utd eventually cruise to an emphatic victory over newly-promoted Ipswich at Old Trafford.

Bruno Fernandes' hat-trick inspires Man Utd to their first win of the season 👏 pic.twitter.com/GNhpUwFUkV

Dorgu looks hungry for a goal as he fires a thunderbolt towards Scherpen’s near post. The Ipswich goalkeeper is up to the task and bats the shot away for a corner.

Man Utd counter as Lammens throws the ball out to Dorgu, who has acres of space to exploit. He tries to pick out Sesko with a cross, but overhits the delivery by some distance. Man Utd look like they could score every time they venture forward.

The Argentine defender won’t want to see this back again... Enciso puts Martinez under pressure and pinches the ball off him. The Ipswich playmaker then sprints towards Lammens and unselfishly slides a pass into Akpom, who slots the ball into an empty net.

There will be eight minutes of added time to end this game.

Man Utd are pushing for a sixth goal and come scarily close to it, but Dorgo’s close-range header is parried away by Scherpen.

Five-star Man Utd are ripping Ipswich apart again. He didn’t score it, but Fernandes is at the heart of this goal. The playmaker floats a delightful ball over Ipswich’s defence for Mbeumo to chase. The forward beats Scherpen to it and lobs the Ipswich goalkeeper. As the ball bounces towards the goal, it kisses the underside of the crossbar. Despite Greaves’ best efforts, he can’t stop the ball from crossing the line.

Carrick orders a triple change as the rain begins to hammer down at Old Trafford. Cunha, Mainoo and Rashford depart for Sesko, Andrey Santos and Dorgu.

Man Utd are close to a fifth goal, but Cunha is denied by Scherpen at his near post. Just before that, Rashford showcased some exceptional skill and nutmegged Diop, but he couldn’t quite get a shot away.

After a flurry of changes for Ipswich amid the chaos, they’ve switched to a back five. Nunez, Lukic and Maeda are all off, with Palacios, Ouattara and Furlong on as the replacements. For Man Utd, Dalot and Shaw are withdrawn for Yoro and Mazraoui.

Fernandes is overflowing with confidence and attempts to lob Scherpen from near the half-way line. His cheeky attempt shaves the roof of the net.

Mbeumo’s blocked effort kindly falls into Fernandes’ path and once again, the Man Utd displays unerring compsure to calmly slide the ball into the bottom corner from close range, leaving Scherpen with no chance. Man Utd are in cruise control now.

"He's the prince of this place!"Bruno Fernandes completes his hat-trick 🎩 pic.twitter.com/KgLlaMcKGR

Rashford meets a clipped cross, but on this occasion, Scherpen is there to make a strong save.

The Portuguese playmaker is the most composed man in Old Trafford. Fernandes coolly sends Scherpen the wrong way and Man Utd now have an invaluable two-goal advantage.

Bruno Fernandes makes it 3-1 to Manchester United from the spot 🎯 pic.twitter.com/vFh7moSSpb

What a nightmare couple of minutes for Ipswich. Mainoo threads a pass through to Cunha, who is cynically apprehended by Greaves’ sliding challenge. It’s all unravelled for Ipswich. It’s a stonewall penalty. Fernandes will take it.

Wave after wave of Man Utd pressure has finally paid off. Man Utd have Ipswich trapped inside their own half as Akpom attempts to chip the ball over Maguire, who blocks it. The defender strides forward and shoots. It’s heading wide, but takes a wicked deflection off Greaves to nestle in the bottom corner. The goal stands after a VAR check.

Harry Maguire's shot cannons in off Jacob Greaves and Manchester United are in front at Old Trafford after a VAR review! 💪 pic.twitter.com/hUdogDQX6k

Some confusion to clear up following the VAR check. The ball struck Maguire’s hand before he shot, but his deflected effort stands because the Man Utd defender wasn’t deemed the ‘immediate goalscorer’ given Greaves’ intervention.

#MUNIPS – 56'The referee's call of goal for Manchester United was checked and confirmed by VAR – with it deemed that Maguire was not the immediate goalscorer after an accidental handball.VAR: "It's an own goal and the accidental handball is not punishable, so we recommend you…

When it’s not your day ... Mbeumo struggled badly offensively and defensively today and that miss from point blank range summed up his afternoon. Plenty of time yet to turn it around of course but he’s got to step it up.

How has that not gone in?! Dalot whips a deep delivery into the box and Rashford does magnificently to keep it in play, volleying the ball back across goal out of Scherpen’s reach. Mbeumo is about a metre from the goal-line and directs Rashford’s assist onto the bar. It’s an extraordinary miss.

"HOW has he missed?!" Bryan Mbeumo misses a golden opportunity to put Man Utd in front 😬 pic.twitter.com/bnZZswysJa

Enciso skips away from Mainoo and drives at Man Utd’s defence. From incredibly far out, he tries his luck, but fires his shot over the bar. Enciso has been a joy to watch so far today.

Enciso showcases some exquisite skill, pirouetting away from Cunha, who brings down the Ipswich playmaker.

We are back under way for the second half. Man Utd are unchanged at the break, while Ipswich have made an alteration, with Akpom on for Emersonn.

Ipswich have looked very useful going forward and richly deserved their opening goal. Fatawu’s dazzling run was rewarded by Davis’ composed finish, but the visitors’ lead didn’t last long. Nunez’s slip proved costly, with Cunha and Fernandes combining to devastating effect, hauling Man Utd level.

A frantic first half comes to a close. It’s been a thoroughly entertaining game of football so far, with Davis and Fernandes both netting via top-quality finishes.

End-to-end stuff at Old Trafford 🤯Leif Davies got the opening goal for Ipswich before Bruno Fernandes equalised for Man Utd. pic.twitter.com/6TAer5eiGJ

There will be two added minutes at the end of this half. Man Utd are pushing for another goal. Can they find a second before the break?

A timely bit of good fortune for United. Cunha takes advantage of poor Nunez’s slip to play an inch perfect pass in behind for the rampaging Fernandes to race clear and fire home.

Disaster for Nunez... Ipswich have a lot of players up the pitch following a long throw-in and the ball is played back to Nunez. The midfielder slips, gifting the hosts a counter attack. Cunha pounces and slides an inch-perfect pass through to the onrushing Fernandes. The Man Utd captain then fires a thunderous effort in at Scherpen’s near post. It’s a magnificent strike. The Ipswich goalkeeper has no chance of saving that. Nunez looks absolutely gutted.

Bruno Fernandes equalises for Manchester United! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/CdEI1REeUD

Fatawu receives a yellow card for clattering into Mbeumo. This game is being played at breakneck speed.

You would have expected Man Utd to come bursting out of the blocks following last week’s disappointment against Hull, but it’s been a really underwhelming display from the hosts so far. Ipswich deserve their lead.

Ipswich nearly make it two! It’s the same combination for Ipswich as Fatawu floats a deep cross into the box for Davis, who makes a late run. Davis meets the delivery from close range, but doesn’t get a clean connection on the strike, allowing Lammens to tip his effort over the bar.

If the first half an hour or so here has done anything, it’s underline how much United need upgrades and reinforcements at full-back. United are in the market for a left back before the window closes and the way Shaw jumped in and then was done by Fatawu for the goal may see those efforts intensified. Davis was criminally unmarked in the middle (what a finish, though, allowing the ball to come across his body then side foot in) with Mbeumo nowhere.

And United haven’t learned from it. Moments later and Fatawu clips in a cross - with not nearly enough pressure from Shaw to shut it out - and Davis is again unmarked at the back with Dalot occupied and Mbeumo ball watching. United are having a real wobble here. Ipswich have been superb. Gary O’Neil will be loving what he is seeing from his side - they’re brave, aggressive and playing with pace and lots of incisive movement.

What a goal from Davis! Fatawu nutmegs Shaw and then outpaces the Man Utd defender. He reaches the byline and picks out the arriving Davis with a pinpoint. Ipswich’s left back then applies a superb finish, directing a superb half-volley in off the bar.

Ipswich STUN Old Trafford! Leif Davis does superbly to volley past Senne Lammens and give Gary O'Neil's side the lead 💥 pic.twitter.com/sJ0XNf8OiT

Mbeumo floats a deep cross towards Rashford at the back post. The Englishman reaches it, but given the power on the delivery, he can’t quite keep it in play.

Man Utd win another free-kick in presentable territory. On this occasion, Fernandes curls his strike into the Ipswich wall.

Davis threads a clever pass trough to Maeda, who creeps in behind Dalot. The winger bursts into the penalty area, before arrowing a powerful attempt towards the far post, but Lammens is there to make a pivotal stop. Ipswich have looked dangerous going forward.

There’s space in behind Diogo Dalot that Ipswich have again exploited, this time with a fine Leif Davis ball for Daizen Maeda to surge in behind the United right back and force a second big save from Lammens. United look a threat going forward but then so do Ipswich, who are picking their moments to break and doing so well.

Rashford tries his luck from long range with a knuckle-ball free-kick. He doesn’t get any accuracy on the strike and it harmlessly flies off target.

This game has exploded into life in the last couple of minutes. End to end action. Scherpen first denying Dalot, then Ipswich going straight down the other end from a long punted clearance and Enciso, holding off Shaw and Mbeumo, forcing a save from Lammens. In keeping with the basketball nature of things, United then went back up the other end, with Cunha overhitting a cross for the onrushing Rashford before Fernandes’ goalbound shot is blocked. It’s certainly entertaining.

Chances at both ends! Firstly, Emersonn hacks Man Utd’s corner away, and Enciso uses his blistering speed to outpace Shaw and Mbeumo, creating a one-on-one with Lammens, who does excellently to smother the shot. Then Man Utd then fly forward straight away and Cunha fires a low delivery across the six-yard box which is marginally out of Rashford’s reach.

Man Utd counter as Fernandes releases Mbeumo with a ball over the top. The hosts recycle the ball well after Rashford crosses, allowing Dalot to cut in or his left foot and bend a curler for the far corner. Scherpen uses every inch of his towering frame to make an eye-catching diving save.

Maeda shows a great turn of pace to breeze past Mbeumo and reach the byline. Under pressure from Dalot, the winger hits his near post cross into Lammens’ hands.

Again, Rashford runs at Ipswich’s backline and cuts inside to reach the penalty area. He tees up Cunha, who smashes an effort well over the bar.

Martinez attempts an ambitious switch of play, aiming for Maguire, but boots the ball straight out of play. O’Shea and Shaw then both go up for a header, with the Ipswich man coming off worse and staying on the ground. He’s back on his feet now and play resumes.

There’s an early roar from the Old Trafford crowd as Rashford gets on the ball and sprints at Ipswich captain O’Shea, who is playing at right back.

Old Trafford welcomes both sides. Can Man Utd find their first win of the Premier League season or will Ipswich spoil the party?

Carlos Baleba has walking out on to the pitch after being introduced at Old Trafford. The new £70m signing from Brighton has been posing for pictures with a shirt and applauding all sections of the ground. He won’t be in action for another two or three weeks most likely owing to an existing ankle injury.

Carlos Baleba is introduced to the Manchester United fans! 👋 pic.twitter.com/QHTCkpe5dz

With kick-off fast approaching, here’s a recap of both line-ups.

Man Utd: Lammens, Dalot, Maguire, Martinez, Shaw, Mainoo, Tielemans, Mbeumo, Fernandes, Rashford, Cunha.

Subs: Darlow, Mazraoui, Zirkzee, Dorgu, Yoro, Santos, Heaven, Sesko, Lacey.

Ipswich: Scherpen, O’Shea, Diop, Greaves, Davis, Nunez, Lukic, Fatawu, Enciso, Maeda, Emersonn.

Subs: Walton, Furlong, Kipre, Walle, McAteer, Palacios, Akpom, Ouattara, Clarke.

"He's a fantastic footballer." Ashley Young discusses Marcus Rashford 🔊 pic.twitter.com/4hYAtx9zZF

Michael Carrick explains the changes to his Man Utd starting XI to face Ipswich 🔴Watch the game live: https://t.co/0AejI4B8dF pic.twitter.com/p9FD36h3OM

Against Hull, Man Utd’s forward line looked way off the pace. In an attempt to stop history repeating itself, Michael Carrick has turned to Marcus Rashford, who is making his first start for the club since the end of 2024.

When Rashford last featured for Man Utd, he was wearing the No.10 shirt. That is now occupied by Mathues Cunha who starts as the central frontman, with Rashford now sporting the No.9.

The hosts will also need captain Bruno Fernandes to deliver. He will levels below his exceptionally high standards last time out, while Bryan Mbeumo also needs to make more of an impact.

It was short and not sweet. Playing in their first top-flight campaign since 2001-02, Ipswich finished 19th with just 22 points under Kieran McKenna.

This time, Gary O’Neil is the boss and they’ve already ticked off one victory thanks to those three points against Sunderland.

Is he the man to guide Ipswich to safety?

Martinez and Dalot are two alterations in Man Utd’s backline, replacing Ayden Heaven and Noussair Mazraoui. Gary Neville feels the club’s defence could let them down this season.

"You can get at them" ❌Gary Neville has concerns over Manchester United's defence for the upcoming season particularly after defeat to Hull 🤔 pic.twitter.com/v3sEjInI2j

First game of the season at Old Trafford for United and one they really need to win after last weekend’s shock defeat at newly promoted Hull City.

Summer signing Andrey Santos has made way for Kobbie Mainoo to partner Youri Tielemans in attack and it’ll be really interesting to see how that midfield pairing dovetail.

It’s a first start at Old Trafford since December 2024 for Marcus Rashford in an attacking looking side. Matheus Cunha is likely to operate as a false nine.

There’s going to be an onus on Rashford and Bryan Mbeumo to provide pace and penetration from out wide and get in behind Ipswich’s defence.

Ipswich enjoyed a great start back in the top flight by winning their opening game against Sunderland and will be out to build on that victory.

Against Hull, Michael Carrick opted for a midfield pivot of Man Utd debutants Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans. However, the pair were completely overran by Hull’s intensity and energy.

Carrick has turned to Kobbie Mainoo as the resolution, with the 21-year-old replacing Andrey Santos. Mainoo went to the World Cup with England this summer, but didn’t play a single minute.

A return to Old Trafford will give Mainoo a chance to remind everyone of his quality.

"I wouldn't say massive concerns, but he will be worried""If Carrick doesn't see a reaction today, there is a problem"The Manchester United players will be under pressure to perform, says Ashley Young 📈 pic.twitter.com/dR6uat4l2P

Man Utd: Lammens, Dalot, Maguire, Martinez, Shaw, Mainoo, Tielemans, Mbeumo, Fernandes, Rashford, Cunha.

Subs: Darlow, Mazraoui, Zirkzee, Dorgu, Yoro, Santos, Heaven, Sesko, Lacey.

Ipswich: Scherpen, O’Shea, Diop, Greaves, Davis, Nunez, Lukic, Fatawu, Enciso, Maeda, Emersonn.

Subs: Walton, Furlong, Kipre, Walle, McAteer, Palacios, Akpom, Ouattara, Clarke.

Gary O’Neil has named an unchanged line-up from the side that beat Sunderland last week. Recent signing Exequiel Palacios is on the bench after joining from Bayer Leverkusen.

Your Town at Old Trafford! ✊ pic.twitter.com/mVMj2LVNvs

Unsurprisingly, Michael Carrick has shuffled his pack after last weekend’s disastrous defeat to Hull. Rashford, Mainoo, Martinez and Dalot all come into the starting X1.

📍 Home.Back where we belong. https://t.co/VbvwRcdF4t pic.twitter.com/37rThnGjyN

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of Sunday’s late Premier League kick-off between Manchester United and Ipswich Town at Old Trafford.

Man Utd suffered an almighty upset last weekend as they slumped to a shock 2-0 defeat against Hull City in Yorkshire. The hosts scored twice after 38 minutes, leaving Michael Carrick’s men with a mountain to climb, but they simply had no answer so Man Utd were shambolic defensively and toothless in attack.

When the fixture list was released, everyone looked at Man Utd’s opening two games against newly-promoted sides as the ideal opportunity for maximum points. But now, there is serious pressure on today’s home team to deliver in front of their fans.

Reflecting on last week’s loss in a press conference ahead of this outing, Carrick said: “I think your success comes from how well you deal with setbacks in the end. In any position, or certainly any sport, particularly this one, going through a season, there are going to be setbacks, sometimes a bit smaller than others. It’s how you deal with that initially, how you react to it and what comes next. I think that ultimately decides what type of team you’re going to become.

“So far, we’ve dealt with those setbacks really well within games and game to game. We had one last week, there’s no getting away from it, and it’s disappointing, but we’re looking to bounce back. We’ve had a good week. The boys have re-focused, learnt from where we could have improved and kept pushing forward.”

Against the odds, Ipswich began their 2026-27 Premier League campaign with a 2-1 comeback victory over Sunderland, with summer signing Emersonn equalising before substitute Jack Clarke found a 90th-minute winner at Portman Road. They followed this game with another triumph at home in midweek, beating Leicester City 3-1 in the League Cup second round.

With all eyes on Man Utd after their stuttering start, Ipswich will see this as an ideal opportunity to ruffle the feathers of a Premier League heavyweight and further dent their sky-high ambitions.

Kick-off is at 16:30, with team news coming shortly.
